text: Singapore has pockets of heritage that deserves more attention and reviving their vibrancy as we re-invent these spaces.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: Our heritage cannot be defined by an infrastructure marker but rather placemaking.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: It has to breathe life with diversity and more interactive activities throughout the day and improve infrastructure that provides ease of movement with comfort of presence under our humid weather.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: To begin, we need to bring the community together including schools, merchants, hotels and community leaders to curate signature concepts that enables raising awareness of the heritage, providing education for more locals while we continue to tout these as tourist destinations.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: The current business mix can also be further improved to attract variety, uniqueness in concepts and having a balance of local and cosmopolitan feel.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: This can incentivise our locals to visit and bring synergies across different business types.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: Space in our tiny island always has many competing needs.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: While we aim to protect and conserve nature biodiversity, how can we expand our limited land space?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: Will using more subterranean space be a possibility for Singapore?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: We have done so for the Jurong Rock Cavern, MRT tunnels and common services tunnels.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: Are we able to move our integrated bus and MRT depots in future below ground and would the revamped Orchard Road or other streets have more underground plans as we go car-lite?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: Will more of the future trends and the land use needs be included in the next Masterplan?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: Singapore’s reputation has been synonymous as a “Garden City”.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: As part of Singapore’s Green Plan (SGP) 2030, a step further was taken to transform Singapore into a “City in Nature”.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: Indeed, with more green spaces interwoven amongst our heartlands, it is not just aesthetically pleasing to the eye and acts as nodes for family and friends to socialise and come together.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: It also acts as buffers against the effects of climate change.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: While all greening efforts are appreciated, one challenge the citizens will have to grapple with is how they can live harmoniously with nature.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: We have heard of incidents of uninvited animals in the household, citizens attacked by animals when they panic and retaliate and some tree species that have been attracting unwanted birds that are creating much nuisance in the neighbourhood.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: As much as we want to progress the effort in giving citizens more access to greenery, we need to utilise more science and technologies to expand the ecological corridor.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: For example, to use heatmaps in identifying the warm spots in existing living environment to decide how to design the green spaces for natural shades that encourage human walking or socialising near their homes, and overlaying the tree varieties to review how the animal species will interact, be attracted or even migrate to the area.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: Ultimately, greening should not bring about inconveniences as an afterthought.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: Can the Minister provide an update on the progress made thus far on this aspect and if there are any areas that we can accelerate the transformation with science-based capabilities?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: Could MND also shed light on how such R&D impact has on the actualisation of our urban sustainability vision?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: What are the opportunities for the community to play a more active role in these transformation efforts?

speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
text: Singapore’ sea space is almost as large as our land space.

speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
text: Given the increasing demands on Singapore’s sea space, for example, for aquaculture and coastal protection measures, it may be important to also better plan for our sea space to meet our future needs.

speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
text: How is the Government incorporating Singapore’s sea space in our Masterplan and long-term plan?

speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
text: Singapore has been experiencing warming temperatures due to climate change and our densely built environment.

speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
text: Passive cooling strategies in newer estates may enable residents to keep cool without resorting to turning on their air-conditioners.

speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
text: But residents in older estates may feel the brunt of warming temperatures.

speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
text: Researchers from the Cooling Singapore project have also identified temperature hot spots in places, such as Geylang and Woodlands.

speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
text: What are the Government’s efforts to ensure that our built environment continues to be liveable for residents in all estates in the face of rising temperatures?

speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
text: How will the findings of the Cooling Singapore project be factored into Singapore’s land use and development plans?

speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
text: Instead, members of the public had to make appointments to view these reports, which can span hundreds of pages, in person during office hours.

speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
text: Singapore’s marine areas will face more pressures due to developments in our aquaculture sector and coastal protection measures.

speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
text: Easier public access to EIA reports can be helpful, for example, in soliciting public perspectives, feedback and suggestions to ensure that our aquaculture and coastal protection activities are implemented, with adequate consideration of the need to conserve our marine biodiversity.

speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
text: How would the Government better engage with the public on these findings?

speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
text: As an island state with limited land, Singapore has to continuously adapt to the changing needs of our society through strategic masterplanning and the constant renewal of our built environment.

speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
text: Tearing down existing concrete buildings to construct new ones will, unavoidably, require cement production, which is the largest single industrial emitter of carbon dioxide, accounting for approximately 8% of global emissions based on a recent peer-reviewed scientific report.

speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
text: An alternative to such a clean-slate development approach is to repurpose existing infrastructure for new uses to minimise both environmental and societal impacts, such as carbon emissions and noise and air pollution.

speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
text: Are there inter-Ministerial strategies to optimise our masterplanning through the adaptive repurposing of our built environment?

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: Can MND provide an update on how key findings of the review will feature in our land use plans?

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: What will be featured in the next Masterplan?

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: Our land has to cater to many competing needs and demands.

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: How can we ensure we will not sacrifice the long-term flexibility for future generations in order to meet immediate demands?

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: Are there any key emergent trends that have changed the assumptions or objectives of our plans?

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: For example, Singapore has set a target to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050.

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: How will that affect our plans and how will that percolate down to other policies?

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: If our plans were to help us accelerate into a low-carbon built environment, we need to consider that buildings account for over 20% of our carbon emissions.

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: The bulk of the buildings is the existing stock of older buildings which may be less energy-efficient.

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: Such a requirement will add on to the cost of operating buildings.

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: How can this be done without overburdening building owners?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: Last year, the URA concluded the Long-Term Plan Review (LTPR).

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: What are the key takeaways from the coastal and marine ecological profiling exercise carried out in tandem with the LTPR and how will these guide URA's plans moving forward?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: In 2020, MND announced its vision to transform Singapore into a city in nature.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: One day, I certainly hope that we can have one million mangrove trees or one million corals restored.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: Could NParks provide an update on the progress of this movement and to what extent does NParks work with partners to ensure that all tree species planted will strengthen ecological resilience and provide more habitats for native biodiversity beyond simply increasing the green cover?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: Could MND please provide an update on the progress of this?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: Given recent human wildlife interactions, including, for example, wild boars and otters, is NParks considering shifting strategies to better tackle this issue?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: How can knowledge better be shared with the wider community as part of everyday norms, as relocation is not a sustainable strategy for the long term in our city in nature and land-scarce Singapore.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: There is also a push for greening industrial estates by optimising greenery, creating forested nodes and strings of connected pocket parts being suggested.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: Could MND also give a progress in this regard?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: This initiative mapped and documented heritage businesses and explored ways to keep traditional trades alive.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: It has documented many heartwarming stories of business owners' deep connection to Kampong Glam, their pride in their craft and their steadfastness amidst changing business environments.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: How does URA plan to incorporate insights from this exercise into heritage conservation and placemaking efforts, particularly in terms of preserving the deep historical and cultural significance of heritage businesses?

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Chairman, property prices tend to be higher in and near the city as well as in neighbourhoods near popular schools.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Many young parents are willing to relocate their homes and pay for more expensive properties just to be near to desired primary schools for the sake of securing places for their children.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: This is a clever strategy by the Government and the ACS Board.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Will there be more similar approaches to spread out the concentration of highly-priced properties to different parts of Singapore?

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Gentrification in older estates, such as Tiong Bahru, has also resulted in a strong desirability of those HDB flats amongst young home owners, despite the short remaining leases.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: What is MND’s strategy to renew ageing precincts in other parts of Singapore?

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: With the climate change crisis, there is urgency for us to go beyond the existing efforts at greening Singapore.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: I observe from the Long-term Plan Review (LTPR) that URA has taken pains to provide more green spaces for play and recreation.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: While I appreciate this as an important step, as many citizens do, too, I also believe that there are many citizens who can and wish to be more participative rather than passive consumers of green spaces.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: How can we create a participative or collaborative model where citizens are actively engaged in realising the “City in Nature”?

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: How can we better allocate our land for various uses to reflect and fulfil Singaporeans’ evolving aspirations and desire for more wellness and balance?

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: The work adjustments that were forced upon us by COVID-19 present us with an opportunity to consider how much space do we really need for offices.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: Personnel that were not essential to be on-site worked from home, freeing up many spaces in the offices.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: In the new era and new economy, do we still need as much land for office spaces?

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: As we rethink what growth means to include well-being, can we not allocate more land away from commercial purposes and towards regenerative and wellness purposes?

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: I proposed the Doughnut Economics model in my Budget debate speech, and it resonated with many Singaporeans who shared how they feel hopeful and vindicated in having their sentiments shared in Parliament – their desire to have a different model of progress.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: Human beings are meant to live as a community and that means we share resources and responsibilities and have one another to lean on.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: In my previous cut, I proposed communal and co-living to foster mutual support and optimise land usage.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: Fostering inter-dependent relationships builds social capital and trust.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: Having social capital and trust and being helpful to one another increases people’s sense of self-worth and self-esteem and security.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: It takes away the need for material possessions to shore up our self-esteem, to acquire status symbols and helps people to feel happier with much lesser.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: Sociologists and anthropologists around the world know this.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: We can greatly reduce wasteful consumption when people have deep contentment and a sense of connectedness in their lives.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: In the same vein, we need to allocate more spaces in Singapore for activities that allow citizens to rebuild our relationship with Nature.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: Human beings are also meant to live in a symbiotic and interdependent relationships with nature.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: When we recognise that we are part of a larger ecosystem, interdependent on one another as well as the flora and fauna that we live amongst, we will constantly be reminded that we are one another’s keeper, making sustainable daily practices of “Using Less, Sharing More and Wasting Not”, a natural way of life.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: It is a way of growing plants and food using nature-based regenerative methods, based on the ethics of “Earth care, People care and fair share”.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: It is a permanent form of agriculture which can be sustained indefinitely.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: It lowers the carbon footprint of food production and at the same time helps the soil used for agriculture to capture carbon from the environment.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: It brings and bonds different members of society together in doing so.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: Many more Singaporeans are now showing a greater interest in growing edibles and being in nature.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: There is societal openness to this, and not just an esoteric interest of a fringe group of enthusiasts.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: We can ride on this momentum and re-introducing nature’s workers such as chickens, bees and fish within our neighbourhoods to produce local food will reduce our reliance on harmful chemicals and machinery that damages Earth.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: Fish in ponds help fertilise crops while eating up mosquito larvae – we do not need fogging and we do not need Wolbachia.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: Our young children will have ample opportunities to interact with Nature, which enhances their physical, intellectual, emotional development.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: As global fuel scarcity increases, countries will choose to prioritise their own people over exporting to us.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: How can we ensure our food security when that happens?

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: There is a little-studied case of the success of Cuba.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: There are scientists in universities, sociologists and even private groups such as Abundant Cities and even passionate individuals like The Tender Gardener Olivia Choong and Urban Jungle Folks led by Ms Michelle Tan who are already rallying Singaporeans in this effort.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: And I believe it is possible to enrol our people to co-create solutions to solve these challenges along the way.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: Where there is a will, there is a way.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Similar trends can be observed with older persons.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Older persons are affected more by specific stresses in later life, example, ongoing loss in capacities and a decline in functional ability which could result in isolation, loneliness and depression.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: In Changi Simei, together with our community partners Changi General Hospital (CGH) and Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD), we have been exploring how the environment can contribute to mental well-being for the young and old in our community.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Studying unused common spaces in the estate, engaging residents to understand needs, observing residents’ rituals and ground stakeholders, we co-created with residents, volunteers and agency partners an open design Art Farm in one of our pocket parks.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: This is now managed by residents and volunteers, with the support of agency partners.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Residents from our public and private estates are involved and enjoy the farm as they wish.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: We believe that better understanding of the design of space and the involvement of community partners and residents in place-making and place-keeping can contribute to the mental well-being of residents across different demographic groups.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: The common shared spaces could include pocket parks, underutilised urban spaces and shared lanes in the private and public estates.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Such spaces create opportunities for new nature spaces for mindful living and activities for the young and old; senior empowerment and volunteerism, youth spaces; inter-generational resident engagement.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: Personally, it has been most beneficial to me, as I can get out for some fresh air and sunlight; and it really improved my overall well-being.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: I am sure this is the case for many others.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: Indeed, during the pandemic, having a park to go to near your home is such a blessing.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: We have our founding leaders to thank for being so steadfast in setting land aside for parks including nature reserves even though Singapore is so land scarce.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: This passion and conviction to safeguard and develop our green spaces has continued through the generations of leaders; and today Singapore is one of the greenest cities in the world.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: Developing and upkeeping a park comes with considerable costs.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: But it is worth it and necessary, particularly so for a densely populated but small island state.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: The pandemic has made Singaporeans even more cherished of our parks and visitorship has risen exponentially.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: It attracted visitors from all over the island.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: MND launched the exciting City in Nature vision three years ago.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: With technology and advancement, new buildings today can use green material and smarter designs to reduce emissions.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: But in a highly built‐up environment like Singapore, we have many mature estates with high concentrations of buildings that are decades old.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Many of these buildings are home to our people.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: I had spoken on this topic in last year's COS debate as well.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: What are the quick wins and achievements so far?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: The use of sensors and artificial intelligence can offer predictive analytics and enable predictive maintenance, which can also identify inefficiencies and help to reduce waste of resources and energy.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: First, leveraging such smart technology at scale could support our journey to go green.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Could the MND share more about how it is leveraging technology to do so?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Also, what else is the MND doing to enhance existing buildings to be more energy efficient and reduce emissions, without having to tear down or affect homes where precious memories are forged?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Xie Yao Quan, take your cuts together.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: What more can be done to bring even more of the community on board these efforts?

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: Since buildings account for over 20% of our carbon emissions, I had asked in last year Committee of Supply about the Government's plans to accelerate our transition to a low-carbon built environment.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: Can MND provide further updates in this regard?

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: How is MND driving research and development in urban sustainability in our context and, at the same time, generating economic opportunities to export our knowledge and capabilities in urban sustainability to the world?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Mr Chairman, COVID-19 has hit the construction sector hard.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We can do more for the built environment sector in the following areas.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Currently, the finalisation of accounts is slow, often taking a few years after project completion.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: New written directions are also being issued, after they complied with original written directions.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Government Procuring Entities (GPEs) should lead by example.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: They should streamline their final account process and certification of VOs and pay contractors promptly.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Each agency also takes a significant time for service diversion, sometimes up to six months.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Moreover, only their own appointed term contractor can carry out the diversionary works.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We must establish timelines and escalation mechanisms or have an effective coordinating body to resolve inter-agency issues.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Third, we need a bigger push to attract our local workforce to take up the higher value-added jobs, such as engineers.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This is to build up resilience when the next pandemic or crisis hits us.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Can MND consider a shorter work week of five days for the sector?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This may seem counterproductive but when workers are well-rested, this promotes an accident-free environment and improves morale and productivity.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: These industries also form a cluster under the Future Economy Council.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Could the Minister elaborate on efforts being made to encourage these sectors to come together to bid for IFM and AFM contracts.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Separately, how can we encourage buyers who are accustomed to tendering for these services separately to start tendering for IFM and AFM contracts instead?

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: And is it possible to introduce incentives to help them craft such tenders?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Certainly, more can be done to green our existing stock of older buildings, which may be less energy efficient.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Can the Ministry share its initiatives and schemes to reduce the carbon footprint of our older buildings?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: At last year's COS, MND announced that it was exploring whether to require building owners to conduct energy audits to improve the energy performance of their buildings.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Will the Ministry proceed to require this of owners, and if so, will there be any Government assistance to help the smaller building owners to perform the energy audits.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Chairman, a key focus area identified in the refreshed Built Environment (BE) Industry Transformation Map (ITM) is integrated planning and design.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: This is necessary as the built sector adopts more pre-fabricated design technologies, design collaboration and digitisation.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Beyond that, it will also shift the job types within the sector to be more knowledge intensive, which will allow us to attract more young Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: It will also strengthen the incentive to create efficiency through this supply chain, through stronger collaboration.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: For example, if future manufacturing contracts has in-built incentive to share the benefits of design improvements for key members along the entire supply chain, the integrated planning and design systems could quickly allow various parties to coordinate design revisions, as well as to objectively measure the time and cost savings due to each party.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Can MND provide more details on its' efforts to drive collaboration at the planning and design stage.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: It is great to hear that Municipal Services Office (MSO)'s Community Advisory Panel (CAP) recommends tackling noises in the community as a first step.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: But is there more that MSO can do to handle neighbor disputes?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Specifically, can MSO do more to resolve disputes that is central around a small group of individuals who exhibit strong anti-social behaviours?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Some of these individuals use feedback channels of agencies to create difficult situations for others and civil servants.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Some of these also harass neighbours and get away with it as they do not breach the legal threshold.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: And some of these people also suffer from mental health issues.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: They need help, but they are not legally obliged to seek it.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Can MND consider getting CAP to set up a framework for Government agencies to proactively identify these individuals, and have a system to intervene to resolve these anti-social behaviours?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Can MND also share what other kind of neighbor disputes will MSO look into prioritising to resolve beyond noise?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: As schools and community exercises have been cited as contributors of community noise, have we consulted the Ministry of Education (MOE) and Health Promotion Board (HPB)?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: Are condo residents required to abide by the quiet hours?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: If so, have the Management Corporation Strata Title (MCST)s been notified?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: Third, we need to explore innovative ways to resolve these problems.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: Are we leveraging technology to monitor and enforce the guidelines?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: Are we learning from other countries on how they solve similar problems?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: Lastly, we should further involve the community to resolve community issues.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: Are there any plans to reintroduce it in some capacity?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: How else is MND encouraging the partnering of the community to redefine social norms, besides joss paper burning practices and community noise?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 3.15 pm.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 2.50 pm until 3.15 pm.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: My colleague, Minister Indranee Rajah will cover our efforts to transform Singapore into a City in Nature, and guide Singapore's future development.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Senior Minister of State Sim Ann will highlight what we are doing to rejuvenate heartland shops and foster gracious communities.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Senior Minister of State Tan Kiat How will speak about the transformation of our Built Environment sector.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And finally, Minister of State Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim will share more about our support for seniors and the more vulnerable members of our society.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: What else are we doing to provide affordable and accessible housing for Singaporeans?

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Our first priority is to catch up on lost time and deliver keys to Singaporeans who have been waiting for their homes.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: My colleagues have been working very hard and we will turn the corner soon.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For Waterway Sunrise II, one of the more badly affected BTO projects, my colleagues at HDB, Expand Construction and Surbana Jurong rotated teams and worked overtime.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: They had to deal with unexpected challenges throughout the pandemic, like finding alternative sources of precast components when Malaysia implemented the movement control order.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Thanks to the team's tremendous effort, we will finally deliver keys to all buyers by the end of this month.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: You may also recall Greatearth, a former main contractor that ran into financial difficulties.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: When that happened, HDB quickly onboarded new contractors within a month.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: My colleagues and I would like to thank Singaporeans for their patience and understanding.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We know the delays have disrupted many of their life plans.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This increased supply should help to alleviate some of the pressures in the rental market, which Mr Louis Chua spoke about.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Households who have been waiting for their keys will leave the rental market for their new homes, and the new homes will provide some additional rental supply.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Second, we have significantly increased the supply of BTO flats.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We launched more than 23,000 flats last year and will launch around the same number this year.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: HDB is now building aggressively and on a very large scale, overseeing almost 100 BTO projects island-wide.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: By 2025, there will be more than 150 concurrent projects.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Some Members have asked why we cannot build even more or build even faster.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I will speak about land preparation while my colleague Senior Minister of State Tan Kiat How will talk about HDB's productivity and innovation journey to build flats that are much taller than before and more comprehensive than in the past.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Land preparation is a long and complex process.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For greenfield sites, we need to ensure that supporting infrastructure like roads and sewers are ready and conduct extensive soil investigations.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For brownfield sites, we may need to relocate existing users, clear existing structures and divert services underground, such as cables and sewers.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We also pay special attention to the ecological and heritage significance of sites to ensure that we develop sensitively and sustainably.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: When needed, we engage extensively and conduct impact studies.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: With the Old Police Academy at Mt Pleasant, for example, studies and engagements began in 2018, seven years before the launch of the first BTO project at this site in 2025.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, a lot of forward planning and preparation is required before we can even begin construction – about five to 10 years of lead time, or even more in some cases.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As Singapore recovers from the pandemic, we should also remember that the pace of construction is going up significantly, not just for HDB but other organisations and businesses too.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Resources, manpower and construction capacity are not without their limits.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We would not have been able to ramp up our BTO supply by 35% in 2022 if not for our pre-pandemic plans to build Shorter Waiting Time flats.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Before COVID-19 hit, we were already planning to launch more flats with shorter waiting times of three years or less.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These are flats that we build ahead of demand, a year or more before they are launched.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And the land preparations would have started even earlier.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, when housing demand rose during the pandemic, we were able to tap on these sites meant for Shorter Waiting Time flats, and bring forward their launch dates and offer them in BTO exercises to meet immediate demand.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: After we address the current supply crunch, we will get back on track to launch more Shorter Waiting Time flats from 2024 onwards.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: By 2025, we plan to return to pre-COVID-19 levels, to launch around 2,000 to 3,000 of such flats per year.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Third, we will have to lend a stronger helping hand to younger married couples and families who are trying to buy their first home.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Throughout our Forward Singapore Housing Conversations, calls to give them more support came across loud and clear.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Today, we already set aside the majority of our BTO flat supply for first-timers – at least 95% of the 4-room or larger flat supply in both mature and non-mature estates.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: First-timers are also given two ballots, compared to one for second-timers.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But first-timers are a diverse group, as they include all eligible Singaporeans who have not enjoyed a housing subsidy before.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: There are some who may have owned private property, some who had purchased a resale flat without taking housing grants and subsidies, as well as couples who are planning to get married.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Among this diverse group, we need to give stronger support to younger married couples and parents.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Indeed, one of the participants in our Forward Singapore Housing Conversations told us that, "It is hard to feel like a family or think about having kids if you don't have your own home." We fully recognise this.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Having a home of their own will provide a stable environment for newly married couples to set up their families, and parents want to give their young children a conducive environment.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: First-timer families with children aged 18 and below, as well as young married couples aged 40 and below, who are embarking on their homeownership journey.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: They must also not have owned or sold any residential property before, nor had the chance to book a flat in the past five years.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is so that we can provide more targeted support for families who want to secure their first home quickly and settle down.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: That said, HDB may exercise flexibility on a case-by-case basis, if there are extenuating circumstances.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For example, I have met adult children who have added themselves as co-owners to their parents' flat so that they could help their parents cope with the mortgage to keep their homes.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: When they apply for a new flat and set up their own families, HDB may consider allowing them to qualify for this priority category.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Some Members – Mr Zhulkarnain, Mr Seah Kian Peng, Ms Foo Mee Har and others – have asked us how we will improve their chances of securing a flat.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, three ballots in total, up from the two that first-timers currently get, when they apply for any flat type in any estate – mature estates, non-mature estates or prime location housing.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Second, we will adjust an existing scheme – the Parenthood Priority Scheme – so that all First-Timer Parents and Married Couples also qualify for this scheme.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The current Parenthood Priority Scheme supports first-timer married couples who have children or who are expecting children.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Under the scheme, up to 30% of the BTO flat supply and 50% of the supply of balance flats will be set aside for eligible applicants.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will now expand the scheme to cover First-Timer Parents and Married Couples too.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: That means that young married couples who do not yet have children can also qualify.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Third, for BTO launches in non-mature estates, we will give First-Timer Parents and Married Couples first priority under the Family and Parenthood Priority Scheme if they apply for a 4-room or smaller flat.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This means that they will be shortlisted ahead of all other applicants who are eligible for the Family and Parenthood Priority Scheme, and stand a higher chance of being invited to select a flat.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Take a young couple, say 26 or 27 years old, who have just ROM-ed (Registry of Marriages) recently.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: They will be considered a first-timer in this enhanced sub-category when they apply for a flat later this year.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Let us say they are considering a 4-room BTO flat in Yishun or Tampines to live near either set of parents.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Regardless which one they choose, they will get three ballot chances from the get-go.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: They will also qualify for the Family and Parenthood Priority Scheme and the Married Child Priority Scheme, which set aside flats for eligible applicants.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And if they choose a 4-room flat in Yishun, which is a non-mature estate, they will be among the first to be shortlisted, across all eligible applicants for the Family and Parenthood Priority Scheme.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, their chances of being invited to select a flat will be substantially higher.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So far, we have observed that virtually all first-timer families have been invited to select a flat within three tries, when they apply for a BTO flat in non-mature estates.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: With these new changes, first-timer parents and married couples should be able to select a flat within fewer attempts, especially if they apply for a 4-room or smaller BTO flat in non-mature estates where demand tends to be more moderate.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Some have asked if fiancé-fiancée couples can receive some extra help too.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We understand that they also hope to settle down quickly, similar to young married couples and families with young children.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But with the tight supply now, even as we are ramping up new supply, let us first help those who are already married or have children, but have yet to secure their first home.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As first-timers, fiancé-fiancée couples will still continue to receive two ballots when they apply for a new HDB flat.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: They will also continue to benefit from the large majority of flats that are set aside for first-timers.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: When they get married or ROM, they will similarly receive extra support to help them secure a flat more quickly.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Currently, 40% of BTO flat applicants who are invited to select a flat decide not to take up the offer.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: When I shared this during our Forward Singapore Housing Conversations, participants were surprised.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: It seemed at odds with what they had heard about strong housing demand.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: They thought that some applicants might be trying their luck, hoping for a good ballot number, for an attractive location.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: My HDB colleagues have also shared that some applicants may be rather selective, wanting only flats, say, on higher floors.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For some, the remaining flats may be out of budget.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For others, they might be considering other housing options, or prefer flats with specific attributes for specific reasons.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Understandably, some would rather give up the opportunity to select a flat now and wait longer for a better flat.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But whatever the reason, such applicants do crowd out other home buyers who may have more pressing needs.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is why we encourage applicants to apply for flats only if they really intend to purchase one because there are other homebuyers who want to buy those flats.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: To reinforce this, our current practice is to issue what we term a "non-selection count", when applicants are invited to book a flat but do not take up the offer.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: After receiving two non-selection counts, first-timers will be considered second-timers for one year when they ballot for a flat.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: They can still apply for a new HDB flat, but the flat allocation quota for second-timers is lower.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As for second-timers who chalk up two non-selection counts, they will not be allowed to participate in HDB sales exercises for a year.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I have heard various suggestions during our Forward Singapore Housing Conversations to bring down the non-selection rate further.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Some suggested raising the BTO application rate from $10 as it is today to $1,000 or more or imposing a financial penalty if applicants do not select a flat and do not have a good reason.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, this is more stringent than what we have in place today.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But, at the same time, we understand that some applicants may have genuine reasons for not selecting a home.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, we want to strike a right balance, because buying a home is a large financial decision.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Some applicants may also turn down the offer to select a flat because their circumstances have changed unexpectedly since they applied for the flat.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Where there are extenuating circumstances, HDB may exercise flexibility to waive the non-selection count, not issue it in the first place.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are announcing them early to give everyone some time to understand how these changes may affect them.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And HDB will also need some time to stress-test and implement the system changes needed for all these moves.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As Deputy Prime Minister Wong has announced recently during his Budget speech, we have increased the CPF Housing Grant for first-timer families, to enhance housing affordability in the resale market.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Some first-timers prefer resale flats because they want to live near their parents or start raising families sooner.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, we have increased the CPF Housing Grant by $30,000 for those who purchase a 4-room or smaller resale flat, and by $10,000 for those who purchase a 5-room or larger resale flat.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Altogether, eligible first-timer families can now receive up to $190,000 when they buy a resale flat.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: To make it easier for buyers who had not completed their resale transaction before this announcement was made, we have extended the enhanced grants to them, so that they would not have to cancel their application and re-apply to qualify for the increased grants.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is unlike grants that are applicable to new BTO flats, which are tied to the prevailing policy at the point of BTO sales launch.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This grant increase was helpful to Mr Zulkhairi, a warehouse logistics trainer and his family of three.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: They recently bought a 3-room resale flat and will receive a total of $130,000 in housing grants.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Zulkhairi shared with us that this will help to lower the monthly mortgage repayments for him and his family.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Some Members, such as Mr Xie Yao Quan, Assoc Prof Jamus Lim, Ms Hazel Poa, Ms Mariam Jaafar and others, voiced concern that this grant may increase resale prices even further.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As Deputy Prime Minister Wong had explained during Budget debate, this was a move that we considered very carefully.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are aware that whenever we increase grants, especially in a buoyant resale environment, there is always this risk.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We decided to move on this, given the current context.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: First, as I mentioned earlier, we have significantly ramped up supply of new BTO flats to meet strong housing demand.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Second, to manage demand and encourage financial prudence, we had introduced two rounds of property cooling measures, which are working their way through the market.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Third, the outlook for the broader economic environment remains extremely uncertain.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The global economy may experience a shallow downturn this year, some analysts say.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mortgage interest rates have increased and could rise further in the coming months from already elevated levels.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: It does not apply universally to the entire resale market, but only a very specific group.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In this economic climate, buyers are growing increasingly price sensitive, so sellers who raise their asking prices run the risk of pricing themselves out of the market.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We hope these moves give first-timers greater assurance about buying their first homes and you can count on our support to set up and raise strong families.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Next, let me share what we are doing to help singles.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Many Members, both present and past spoke about this, like Miss Cheryl Chan, Ms Carrie Tan, Mr Louis Chua, Mr Xie Yao Quan, Ms Heng Ting Ru, Ms Joan Pereira, Miss Rachel Ong and many others.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: While we support families strongly, we recognise that society continues to change.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: More Singaporeans want to live apart from their parents before settling down.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: There are also singles who help to take care of their ageing parents but hope to have a place of their own.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Others are caregivers of older parents and want to have their own space.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Their housing aspirations and needs are important too.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And we have been making changes to better support them over the years.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We first introduced the Single Singapore Citizen Scheme in 1991, when singles could purchase HDB resale flats.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: From 2013, singles could also apply for a new 2-room Flexi flat.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Then, in 2018, we increased the Proximity Housing Grant for singles who wanted to buy a resale flat to live with their parents.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We also extended it to singles who wanted to buy a resale flat of their own, but remain near their parents, instead of living with their parents, often for caregiving reasons.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In August last year, we increased the allocation quota for singles buying 2-room Flexi flats from 50% to 65%, to improve their chances of securing a home.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are glad to know that this provides more help to singles, like Ms Cheryll Yeo, to purchase flats of their own.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Her new home is near her parents' place in Hougang, so she will receive the $10,000 Proximity Housing Grant too.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: During our Forward Singapore Housing Conversations, many singles, young and older, shared their challenges, perspectives and suggestions with us.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are closely studying what they have told us, to see how else we can support their housing aspirations, including through co-living models or other types of housing arrangements as Ms Carrie Tan and Mr Xie Yao Quan have suggested.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Over the years, we have introduced various upgrading programmes to help them age-in-place.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: To go a step further, MND, MOH and HDB have jointly developed a new housing type, the Community Care Apartment, or CCA.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is a fairly new housing-plus-care option for seniors.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have launched two pilots, at Bukit Batok and at Queenstown, which were well-subscribed.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Given the positive response so far, we are developing a pipeline of Community Care Apartments in different locations across Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are working out the details and will share more later this year.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will also continue to refine the Community Care Apartment model as we gain experience, especially after our first residents move in next year.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: My colleague, Minister of State Faishal Ibrahim will elaborate more on our efforts to help seniors age-in-place later.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: About 85% of our low-income households in Singapore own their homes.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We achieve this high rate of ownership by pricing our flats so that lower-income households can afford them too.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We also adopt a progressive approach, with more housing grants to support those with lower incomes.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For those who are not yet ready for home ownership, we provide highly subsidised rental flats as a social safety net.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We recognise that some of these households may face other complex, interlocking challenges.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, we pair rental housing with social support, to make sure that tenants receive the support that they need to achieve stability, self-reliance and social mobility.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Many Members have asked about our efforts to support and uplift our rental tenants, and Minister of State Faishal will share more later.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As I have said before, our public housing system is not perfect.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We must learn from our experiences, continually improve and enhance our system for Singaporeans, and I thank Members for their thoughtful suggestions.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For example, we used to have the Registration for Flats System, or RFS.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This was basically a queue system – HDB built flats based on the number of applicants in the queue and flats were allocated on a first-come, first-served basis.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But when the Asian Financial Crisis hit in 1997, housing demand plummeted.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The queue disappeared, leaving HDB with 31,000 unsold flats which took many years to sell.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: It had a very serious impact on the value of existing homes in the resale market, affecting existing home owners.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, the challenges with the RFS were plain to see then.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We acknowledge then that it could not cope with sharp and sudden shifts in demand.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, in 2002, we decided to replace it with the Build-To-Order (BTO) model, but we did not stop there.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Over the years, we continued to refine our system.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Today, we have a more comprehensive model, which is still developing, comprising of BTO flats, Shorter Waiting Time flats, Sale of Balance flats (SBF) and flats that are offered under open booking.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This combination allows us to more dynamically adjust our building plans in response to demand.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: If demand surges, including suddenly like now during a crisis, we ramp up our main BTO pipeline and tap on our Shorter Waiting Time flat pipeline to meet immediate needs.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And with a greater number of Shorter Waiting Time flats in future, this will be a more effective buffer.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: If demand falls, we can scale back the BTO pipeline responsively and allow homebuyers to book unselected flats from earlier launches through SBF or through open booking exercises, to minimise the potential for oversupply.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have also fine-tuned our current system with priority schemes and ballot chances, so that we can provide additional support to specific groups of buyers, like the First-Timer Parents and Married Couples we talked about earlier.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In comparison, the allocation of flats under RFS was much more basic.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The current system may not always work perfectly, and we will continue to adjust and calibrate along the way.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But it does seek to strike a reasonable balance across multiple objectives – fairness and efficiency in allocating flats, fiscal prudence and responsiveness to demand.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Compared to its predecessors, the pure BTO model and the RFS model, I think it is a clear improvement.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Now, on the affordability of flats and fiscal sustainability.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We set prices for BTO flats with affordability in mind.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: When incomes and prices go up together, flats will remain affordable and we may not need to increase market discounts or subsidies so much.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We also keep our market discounts and subsidies targeted for first-timers as well as households with lower incomes.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And we are open to new approaches, like the Prime Location Public Housing Model, which we put in place after lots of engagement, which prevents flat buyers from benefiting from higher market discounts which later translate into excessive windfall gains.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Progress Singapore Party (PSP) and the Workers' Party (WP) have offered suggestions on how flats can be made even cheaper than today.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have debated them extensively in the very recent Housing Motion, and we have carefully explained the difficulties that we see with these ideas, so I will not delve into them today.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Henry Kwek, Mr Louis Chua, Ms Hazel Poa and Ms Foo Mee Har also raised some suggestions about housing loans.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We use the CPF Ordinary Account (OA) interest rate as a peg, to give borrowers greater stability and certainty, since most service their mortgage repayments using their CPF OA savings.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Nonetheless, for homeowners who face difficulties keeping up with their mortgage instalments, HDB has various financial assistance measures in place to help them.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: HDB also provides one-to-one financial counselling to homeowners who are in arrears and will offer appropriate measures, depending on their situation, to help them.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We do not expect this to adversely affect a significant proportion of first-time homebuyers.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The significant grants we provide, especially for lower-income first-timers, allows them to offset the cash component of their flats.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Nevertheless, I assure Ms Foo that we will keep watch and take this into consideration as we review our policies.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Chairman, allow me to speak in Mandarin, please.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: (In Mandarin):   The Government is committed to providing good homes for Singaporeans through various stages of life from your first home into your silver years.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We understand that many are anxious about the current housing situation.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: You might wonder, will your children be able to afford a home?

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: COVID-19 has significantly derailed our building plans, but we are getting back on track.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Apart from ramping up the BTO supply, we will do even more to help first-timers to secure a flat.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: If your children are first-timers, have children or are a young married couple aged 40 and below, and have never owned any residential property or had the chance to book a flat in the past five years, we will help them to secure a flat more quickly.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Second, we previously had the Parenthood Priority Scheme, where we set aside up to 30% of the 3-room or larger BTO flat supply for married couples with children.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will now expand this programme and rename it to the Family and Parenthood Priority Scheme.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As with earlier generations of Singaporeans, the Government will help your children to buy their first homes, and support them as they set up and raise their families.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will take care of our seniors' housing needs too.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are launching a third Community Care Apartment at Bedok later this year.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is an assisted living option designed for seniors.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This programme offers senior-friendly flat features, care services and social activities, so that seniors can enjoy their silver years with peace of mind.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: (In English): Looking ahead, we are making ambitious, exciting moves to create space for our future needs, for our future generations, including in housing.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have already opened up new towns and housing areas in Tengah, in Miltonia and Ulu Pandan East, to offer some 36,000 HDB flats.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These plans were set in motion over a decade ago, when we started planning for the relocation of the Paya Lebar Airbase, Tanjong Pagar and Pasir Panjang ports.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are also working on our plans for the Voluntary Early Redevelopment Scheme, or VERS, so that we can redevelop our towns in a sustainable manner and ensure equitable housing across generations.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As has been the hallmark of this Government, we will always look ahead to plan sustainably.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will continue to provide good homes for our people; and we will work closely with Singaporeans to ensure that the future of Singapore remains bright, inclusive and liveable.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Chairman, over the last 58 years, we made the journey from mudflats to Metropolis.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Now, coming out of a global pandemic, we are poised to embark on the next stage of our city's transformation.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Building on the ideas, hopes, aspirations and dreams of Singaporeans, conveyed to us through extensive engagements, as well as based on Government planning, future Singapore will be one that is inclusive, sustainable, resilient and endearing.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Planning for the future requires us to think long term.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This included an extensive engagement with Singaporeans to hear their thoughts on these strategies, as Senior Minister of State Sim Ann mentioned in the COS 2022.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao, Miss Cheryl Chan and Ms Nadia Samdin have asked for an update on this.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Through this process, we found that we sometimes have different needs and aspirations, and therefore, must make trade-offs.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It is part and parcel of land use planning, given that Singapore has limited land.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Our collective aspirations and potential strategies to achieve them, were featured in URA's Space for our Dreams exhibition in 2022, which was visited by close to 50,000 people, with 150,000 views on URA's website.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: First, it is evident that Singaporeans take pride in our identity and heritage.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: While we cannot conserve each and every older building, we nevertheless want to feel that sense of familiarity and connection as we walk through our streets.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Today, we already carefully consider how to safeguard our heritage as a key part of urban planning.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Second, it is clear that we love nature and greenery.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But, at the same time, there is both need and demand for development.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin asked how we would balance the two.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We take a science-based approach to identify ecologically important sites and prioritise them for conservation.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For example, through National Parks Board (NParks)'s Ecological Profiling Exercise, we have gained a better understanding of Singapore's ecological connectivity and have identified key ecological corridors on our land and in our waters.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: However, given our physical constraints, we need to balance demands across a wide variety of needs, including housing, community amenities and workplaces.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: There may be some greenfield sites that we need to safeguard as options for development.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But Singaporeans can be assured that any decision to proceed will only be made after we have carefully studied the trade-offs and alternatives in close coordination with the relevant agencies.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Where necessary, we will also undertake environmental studies and formulate mitigation measures.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Government will also engage and involve stakeholders.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In response to Prof Koh Lian Pin, for proposed developments that require an Environmental Impact Assessment, we seek views from academics, stakeholder groups and the public on the findings where applicable.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The reports are also made publicly available online, unless there are reasons to maintain confidentiality, such as security considerations.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In these cases, we will consider whether the full report can be made public and the disclosure modality, such as, for example, making it available for hard copy viewing.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: And we do recognise that some may face difficulties accessing hardcopy reports.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Where possible, we will provide accommodations, such as by extending the duration of the public feedback period.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: All feedback is carefully considered and incorporated into the final report and our plans where relevant.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Third, some participants shared concerns on how Singapore will adapt to the increasingly complex and ambiguous global environment, something which Mr Cheng Hsing Yao also spoke about.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To cater for the uncertainties of the future, we continuously monitor trends, such as an ageing population, to evolving geopolitical tensions, and shifts in the global economic outlook.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This enables us to consider a range of possibilities and plan ahead to enhance our resilience.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Ms Carrie Tan suggested we review the allocation of land to various uses, such as residential and commercial, to factor in evolving trends, such as changes to live-work patterns.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Indeed, this is something we currently do and will continue to do.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is so that we can adjust the mix of uses to respond to changing trends and needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Long-Term Plan Review, as the name indicates, sets out our goals in the long-term, that is, to say, a 50-year timeframe or so.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Masterplan presents an opportunity to plan ways to improve our living environment together.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In response to Mr Cheng Hsing Yao and Miss Cheryl Chan, URA is currently working on the key ideas, but allow me share some of the strategies that the Masterplan will be built upon.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: First, the Masterplan will be centred on liveable towns.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As we plan for a new generation of towns, such as the ones that Paya Lebar Airbase will make way for and rejuvenate our older ones, we will pay close attention to making them more liveable for everyone.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Ms Poh Li San asked about plans to spread out amenities to better serve residential estates across Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It remains our priority to make every housing estate a desirable place to live in.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
