text: We will continue to ensure that our estates are planned with a range of housing options, served by a wide variety of amenities that meet our residents' needs and preferences and are highly accessible.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Second, the Masterplan will work within our land and resource constraints, a necessity for a small city like Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: One way is to recycle our brownfield sites.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: There are also ongoing efforts to increase and optimise our underground space, as highlighted by Miss Cheryl Chan.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Where possible, we place infrastructure, such as transport, utilities and storage spaces underground to free up aboveground space for housing, recreational spaces and other people-centric uses.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will also repurpose existing buildings, as Prof Koh Lian Pin highlighted.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Today, we have incentives to encourage adaptive reuse.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: State properties are put to various uses, from residential to lifestyle.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: During COVID-19, many were activated as quarantine facilities.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: There are also incentives for owners who renovate their conserved buildings to meet modern uses while enhancing the building character, such as additional floor area and tax concessions.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: However, there will still be situations where redevelopment is needed.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In such cases, we have incentives to minimise emissions, such as BCA's Green Mark certification scheme that recognises redevelopment projects that conserve existing structures and reuse or recycle demolished materials.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Several Members also suggested repurposing under-utilised spaces for new uses.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim asked if the lowest floor of multi-storey car parks can be repurposed for bicycle parking, echoing a similar call made earlier by Mr Edward Chia in November 2022.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For some public housing developments, bicycle parking is provided at the void deck for our residents' convenience.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Multi-storey carparks with under-utilised space are currently used for various activities.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We do not generally co-locate bicycle parking in car parks as this could pose safety issues to cyclists, especially where cars and bicycles have to use the same lanes.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: However, if a request is made by any precinct for this, HDB will consider on a case-by-case basis, taking into consideration other competing uses for the carparks and whether the safety concerns and any other relevant considerations can be adequately addressed.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Ms Jessica Tan, Ms Carrie Tan, Miss Cheryl Chan and Mr Liang Eng Hwa suggested partnering the community to co-create shared spaces, such as permaculture plots or pilots.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Today, there are opportunities for Singaporeans to co-create community projects, leveraging URA's and HDB's Lively Places Programme.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Many projects are in under-utilised spaces, including a void deck garden in Bishan.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For permaculture farms to meaningfully enhance food security, they should be done on a commercial scale.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Given the sizeable amount of land required, it is more practical to encourage community gardeners to adopt permaculture principles.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Nevertheless, Town Councils have the autonomy to determine how common property can be utilised, subject to our laws and HDB's consent.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are happy to consider proposals that enhance food security and sustainability, where appropriate.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As Prof Koh Lian Pin highlighted, there are diverse and competing needs for our sea space as well.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We carefully plan our sea space to meet Singapore's needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Today, most sea space within our port limits are used by the maritime and port industry.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We also set aside space for other uses, including marine biodiversity conservation, aquaculture, utilities and recreation.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To optimise our sea space, we will continue working with relevant stakeholders to explore co-locating synergistic uses, such as siting of solar panels together with fish farms along the East Johor Straits.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These ideas, plans and strategies will eventually culminate in URA's presentation of their next draft Masterplan, which will be open for public feedback.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I strongly encourage all Singaporeans to participate and share your views.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Next, let me zoom in one level deeper and speak about our plans to rejuvenate HDB estates, which are a big part of our residents' day-to-day lived experiences.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As our nation gets older, so do our towns.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But this does not mean that they cannot continue to be vibrant and liveable.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In response to Ms Poh Li San, HDB crowdsources ideas from residents to renew and rejuvenate existing HDB towns and estates under the Remaking Our Heartland programme.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This spans from upgrading our town and Neighbourhood Centres to opening new community spaces and parks.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Ms Joan Pereira and Mr Ang Wei Neng asked about plans to maintain and upgrade older flats.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In between, we provide support to flat owners for in-flat maintenance issues, such as repairing ceiling leaks under the Goodwill Repair Assistance.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Besides upgrading, redevelopment is another way to rejuvenate older areas.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As Minister Desmond has mentioned earlier, we are also working on our plans for the Voluntary Early Redevelopment Scheme, or VERS.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: More households will be able to benefit from redevelopment before their leases expire and we can renew our towns progressively and create a refreshed living environment with new homes and updated amenities for residents.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will share more details with Singaporeans when ready.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Several Members also asked about HIP's drying racks.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The external retractable clothes drying rack that Mr Ang Wei Neng spoke about is designed to maximise laundry capacity while ensuring user safety.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Each of the six poles in the rack measures up to 1.7 metres in usable length, to accommodate large items like bedsheets.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: HDB will continue ways to look for ways to increase the rack's laundry capacity.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: On Mr Muhamad Faisal Abdul Manap's suggestion to extend the installation of HIP's laundry hanging rack to flats which do not qualify for the programme, we can consider this when there is sufficient demand.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Allow me to respond to Mr Ang Wei Neng and Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong's cuts on lift upgrading.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is due to technical and site constraints or high costs, some of which exceed $100,000 per unit.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: HDB continues to explore technical methods, though these are still nascent.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will also continue to review requests for lift upgrading, bearing in mind costs, space constraints and technical feasibility.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: A key condition for this grant is that residents need direct lift access due to medical or mobility issues.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Of those who have applied, the approval rate is high, at close to 90%.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As our residents aged, we do expect take-up to increase as they face medical or mobility conditions.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Flat owners who have bought another flat with the grants can sell their existing flat on the open market.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Hence, there is no need for HDB to buy them back.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: If they have difficulties selling the existing flat, HDB can grant a time extension on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: HDB will continue to monitor the situation and assess if further enhancements to the grant are necessary.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Prof Koh Lian Pin asked about our efforts to keep older estates cool as temperatures rise and how we will use the findings from Cooling Singapore 2.0.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: HDB has several initiatives under the Green Towns Programme to reduce ambient temperatures, such as: Introducing greenery to the top decks of selected multi-storey car parks in the form of urban farms, community gardens or rooftop greenery.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: There is also an ongoing pilot on cool paint.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Where possible, such as for newer towns like Tengah, we adopt new technologies such as the Centralised Cooling System, which provides a more energy-efficient cooling solution than conventional air-conditioning systems.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will continue to invest in R&D to deepen our knowledge on urban heat.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This includes Cooling Singapore 2.0, an ongoing project where a digital model simulating our urban climate will help us understand the impact of urban heat locally and assess heat mitigation strategies.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Chong Kee Hiong spoke about the need to educate residents on fire safety and provide safety features in HDB flats and estates.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Since 2018, SCDF’s Fire Code requires every new flat and existing flat undergoing major renovation to install fire alarms.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As optional improvements under HIP, HDB also offers installations of a Home Fire Alarm Device.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: HDB and SCDF are further embarking on a trial to place and maintain one fire extinguisher at a lift lobby of every two HDB blocks.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Out of the 934 cases of residential fire last year, 783 took place in HDB flats, which reflects the proportion of public housing in Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Today, SCDF conducts public education campaigns, including door-to-door engagements with residents and educating new homeowners on fire safety together with HDB.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Currently, all flat owners who are taking or have an existing HDB loan to buy their flats are required to be covered under basic fire insurance.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This vision is a key pillar of the Singapore Green Plan 2030.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It underscores our strong desire to conserve and extend our natural capital – for the benefit of the environment and for the benefit of our people.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Miss Cheryl Chan asked for updates on our progress on this front.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: First, we have continued to establish new green spaces and to enhance existing ones.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For instance, last November, we opened the Rifle Range Nature Park.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It serves as an ecological buffer to protect the rich biodiversity in the Bukit Timah Nature Reserve and creates more opportunities for families to enjoy nature-based recreation.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Between now and 2030, we have six more nature parks in the pipeline that Singaporeans can look forward to.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This includes the Lim Chu Kang Nature Park, which we will be opening later this year.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It will feature a variety of natural habitats such as mangroves, woodlands and grasslands, as well as a restored colonial-era bungalow for those who lover heritage.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Singaporeans can also soon enjoy the northern section of the Lakeside Garden in Jurong Lake Gardens.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It will offer a youth park with skating facilities and panoramic views across Jurong Lake.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are also enhancing our existing green spaces to make them more inclusive.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Second, we are pressing on with efforts to restore nature into our urban landscape.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Today, we have around 155 hectares of skyrise greenery, equivalent to almost 220 football fields.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are on track to meet our target of 200 hectares by 2030.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Ms Nadia Samdin asked about our efforts to green industrial estates.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: By 2030, these estates will have around 260,000 trees.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These will cool the environment and beautify the area for the people who work there.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Third, we are strengthening the connectivity between green spaces.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For example, we opened the northern stretch of the Rail Corridor last month, completing over 21 kilometres of green, continuous north-south connectivity.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In total, we have completed over 180 kilometres of Nature Ways and 375 kilometres of park connectors, putting us on track to achieve our goal for all households to be within a 10-minute walk from a park by 2030.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This increases Singaporeans’ access to nature and strengthens our ecosystems’ resilience, by facilitating the movement of biodiversity between habitats.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This includes the endemic Singapore Ginger and the Singapore Freshwater Crab.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have also restored and enhanced over 30 hectares of forest, coastal, and marine habitats, well ahead of our target to do so by 2030.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This was made possible through the contributions of our volunteers, who help with planting native trees and shrubs, and removing invasive species.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As we push on with our greening efforts, Mr Liang Eng Hwa and Mr Xie Yao Quan have asked how we can involve even more members of the community.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This year marks 60 years since then-Prime Minister Mr Lee Kuan Yew kickstarted our greening journey by launching our first nation-wide tree-planting campaign in 1963.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Under the OneMillionTrees movement, we have partnered more than 75,000 members of the community to plant over 500,000 trees since 2020.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have planted native rainforest species in our forests to strengthen the ecological resilience of these habitats, so that they can better support our native biodiversity.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The planted trees also help to intensify greenery and strengthen ecological connectivity along our streetscapes, Nature Ways and park connectors.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To commemorate this milestone year, we will create more tree-planting opportunities under the OneMillionTrees movement and we hope that you will join us in celebrating this milestone.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will also continue to engage Singaporeans on the conservation and celebration of our natural heritage.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Through our City in Nature Conversations, we were inspired by members of the community who shared and worked on ideas to encourage more residents to participate in our efforts.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will reach out to more youths through platforms such as our Youth Stewards for Nature programme, to nurture future volunteers and stewards of our natural heritage.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Xie Yao Quan and Miss Cheryl Chan have also asked about our research and development (R&D) efforts in urban sustainability.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are collaborating closely with industry and academic partners to support our key initiatives under the Singapore Green Plan 2030, including our City in Nature ambitions.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: One looks at developing ecological and microbial solutions to enhance the resilience of coral reefs to climate change.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: So, I look forward to active participation in our grant call.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The years ahead are going to be very exciting ones as we shape our future city together.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The MND family looks forward to working with all Singaporeans on this transformation journey and to making Singapore a place we are proud to call home.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Members for their cuts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Building an endearing home for Singaporeans goes beyond the hardware or infrastructure development.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It is about supporting our residents with accessible and affordable amenities, preserving community ties and collective memories, and building a gracious living environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I will speak about three areas that MND will do more in, in collaboration with the people and private sectors: first, transforming our heartland shops to be more vibrant and better serve the needs of the community; second, ensuring that food and beverage continues to be affordable and accessible; and third, creating a quality living environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: First, let me share our plans to transform heartland shops.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa, Mr Xie Yao Quan, and Mr Pritam Singh spoke on this subject.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We all agree on the importance and relevance of heartland shops.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The question is how to ensure that residents’ and shoppers’ diverse needs are met while also being supportive of businesses and the spirit of enterprise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is not something that the Government alone can determine.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In response, HDB and Enterprise Singapore will launch a new roadmap of efforts to support the rejuvenation and transformation of heartland shops.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Minister of State Low Yen Ling has spoken on Enterprise SG's moves during Ministry of Trade and Industry's Committee of Supply, and I wish to now address initiatives that MND and HDB will undertake as part of this joint effort.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: First, part of this transformation is to give existing HDB shop precincts a greater role in incubating startups.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The heartlands have been the birthplace of more than a few successful Singapore brands.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Charles and Keith, for example, started from a shoe shop in Ang Mo Kio Central in the 1990s, and now has hundreds of stores worldwide.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We believe more such brands can be nurtured in our heartlands.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We are excited to work with Enterprise SG to facilitate this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Entrepreneurs will, therefore, have a platform to test out innovative and different models of service in a more conducive environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Second, we will enhance the Revitalisation of Shops (ROS) scheme to support the transformation of our HDB shop precincts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This will make it easier for precincts to benefit from rejuvenation works.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In response to Mr Liang Eng Hwa, HDB will be shortlisting sites for the ROS over the next few months before inviting local merchant associations to apply.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To minimise disruption, areas that have been selected for or are undergoing other HDB upgrading programmes, or where the Town Councils have plans for repair and redecoration works, will be prioritised.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Priority may also be given to older neighbourhoods that have not yet undergone ROS upgrading.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To Mr Pritam Singh's feedback on the use of outdoor display areas, or ODA for short, HDB has issued guidelines on the management of these areas, but Town Councils are empowered to manage them as part of common property.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The foremost consideration is to ensure public safety and tidiness of these common areas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Hence, we require clear and open passageways, and for the local shop operator to manage the ODA operations directly outside the shop.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Under current guidelines, unrelated trades are not allowed at ODAs as these are primarily meant as an extension of the existing shops' operations to draw crowds into the shops.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Itinerant retailers can bring added vibrancy and variety to the HDB retail scene, but the proliferation of commercial activities, if left unchecked, might lead to excessive noise and crowding, as well as unfair competition to existing shopkeepers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It is the role of Town Councils to enforce against the improper use of ODAs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We know that Town Councils have many roles and responsibilities to discharge, and we leave it to the Town Councils to decide how to prioritise amongst these different responsibilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: If there are instances of violation that need to be reported, please inform HDB and we will look into it.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Third, we will support our heartland businesses to employ locals and to keep food affordable for residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These efforts will help make HDB heartlands even more inclusive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: There is the potential for heartland shops to provide a variety of employment opportunities close to our homes, specifically through social enterprises and businesses with inclusive hiring practices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Xie Yao Quan has spoken on this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These employment opportunities bring not just an income, but a sense of self-reliance and dignity to vulnerable individuals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We want to support more businesses in making these opportunities available and uplifting more lives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We have seen good results from the 24 beneficiaries of the Social Enterprise Scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We hope these measures help to increase employment opportunities for our seniors and persons with disabilities or special needs in our community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Next, let me talk about the accessibility of amenities and of affordable food in particular, a subject raised by Mr Louis Chua, Mr Henry Kwek, Mr Xie Yao Quan, Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Assoc Prof Jamus Lim.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Today, all HDB towns are planned with a variety of facilities and amenities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I should add that hawker centre placement is done by NEA, and, just now, during MSE's COS debate, the subject of hawker centres and the prices of meals available at hawker centres have been given quite extensive treatment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Commercial facilities are injected based on the needs of residents, while also considering the viability of operators.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In built-up sites, HDB will assess and facilitate requests for new commercial facilities on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For example, in Sengkang, URA and the relevant agencies are currently reviewing plans to further develop the Sengkang Town Centre.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The agencies will reply to Mr Louis Chua.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Most residents can access commercial facilities with a food court or eating house within 400 metres from their homes or an approximately five to 10 minutes' walk.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Beyond accessibility, we hear ground concerns about rising costs of living and want to proactively ensure that our residents can continue to access affordable cooked food options within neighbourhoods.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In 2018, HDB launched the PQM framework, after considering various mechanisms, where new tenders of rental coffee shops were required to provide six budget meals as well as a budget drink.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Operators who successfully tendered for HDB coffee shops under this framework, typically provided budget food options averaging $3.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The rentals under price-quality tenders were also, generally, lower than before, under pure price bidding tenders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Tenderers, too, shared that they appreciated the opportunity to compete on quality rather than on price alone.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As a start, we will require these coffee shops to provide budget prices for four meals, instead of six, and two drinks as a condition for renewal.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The budget meal and drink prices will be benchmarked against economically-priced F&B offerings in nearby neighbourhood coffee shops.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will consult operators and remain flexible in assessing their proposed prices, bearing in mind business sustainability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To help rental coffee shop operators and stallholders with this transition, they will be offered a rental discount of 5% off their renewal rents for one year, from the time the new requirements are in place.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: MND and HDB will engage industry players on the budget meal provision and related matters soon.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: First of all, our experience with the PQM framework, as I have shared, has shown that lower rents can be achieved, compared to price-based tenders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: When it comes to the factors driving the prices of meals in coffee shops, apart from rents, there are other factors alluded to just now by Senior Minister of State Amy Khor during MSE's COS debate, and these are factors that, I believe, apply not just to hawker centres but also to eating houses or coffee shops and these would be food ingredients, as well as expenditure on manpower.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: So, even if we were to focus primarily on rents, that alone might not guarantee lower or budget meal prices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: So, this is the reason why HDB has decided to get to the heart of the matter by expanding the budget meal regime, and we will be doing so for all rental coffee shops.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We also intend to monitor adherence of the coffee shops that have moved on to the budget meal regime.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: There is also the question of sold coffee shops.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: What do we do about the sold coffee shops?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Well, we have just, very recently, extended invitations to eating house chain executives and I will be speaking with them and engaging them on the importance of ensuring affordable meal options, notwithstanding the fact that they are operating out of sold coffee shops, Next, let me talk about how MND intends to support the maintenance of a quality living environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Murali Pillai suggested that there is a need to review funding for Town Councils, given the increasing overall maintenance costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Specifically, the automated fire-rated roller shutters in Mr Murali's estate were installed to meet fire safety requirements due to site-specific considerations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We hear the views shared previously by Mr Murali and other Members on how design features of HDB estates must not only be attractive but also practical and cost-effective from the viewpoint of long-term maintenance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Municipal Services Office (MSO) has also been engaging Town Councils on their views on specific design features and will be presenting these to HDB.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Government agencies also share best practices with Town Councils to support their maintenance operations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For example, NParks shares advice on how to reduce bird-related disamenities, such as by growing plant species that are less attractive to pest birds.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: MND has been closely monitoring the larger macroeconomic environment and cost-drivers affecting Town Councils.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As costs of maintenance rise over time, we know Town Councils have been doing their part to raise service and conservancy charges (S&CC) periodically, even as they continually seek to realise cost savings and improve productivity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is part and parcel of discharging Town Councils' responsibilities for running their towns sustainably.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: On its part, the Government acknowledges that some of the cost increases Town Councils are facing now are sharp and steep, due to external factors, such as the spike in energy prices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Since 2014, the MSO, in partnership with agencies and Town Councils, has made good progress in improving the delivery of municipal services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Through digital services, such as the OneService App, Kaki the Chatbot, and with OneService functions now available in LifeSG, residents can conveniently provide feedback on their living environment to the Government.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We have become better at responding to cases, but there remains a subset of municipal issues that are socio-behavioural in nature.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These arise from differences in how we relate to one another and cannot be resolved by the Government alone.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: They require us to partner the community and refresh our social norms to better reflect society's changing and diverse preferences.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Our experience with the Alliance for Action (AfA) on Norms for Joss Paper Burning shows that promising results can be achieved if we find the right approach to go about norms resetting.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Joss paper burning is a longstanding cultural practice in our Chinese community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Practices can be updated, however, and disamenities like excess smoke and ash reduced, if practitioners adopt minor changes to what they do.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The AfA, led by leaders and cultural experts from the Chinese community, developed public education campaigns for last year’s Seventh Lunar Month and the recent Lunar New Year that directly address the mindset and intentions of practitioners, correct misconceptions and demonstrate responsible burning practices in HDB estates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked how MSO will be leveraging technology and partnering the community to address social norms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Social norms also play a pivotal role in the complex and subjective issue of neighbourhood noise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Last year, I announced the formation of the Community Advisory Panel on Neighbourhood Noise, or CAP for short, as part of a holistic response to address this issue.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The panel engaged the community to establish an understanding of what kinds of noise are acceptable or unacceptable in a residential setting and has recommended community norms for noise management to the Government.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The panel highlighted the importance of residents being able to engage neighbours to resolve issues amicably in the first instance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The panel also identified a list of considerate behaviours that residents can adopt to manage noise that is created in our daily lives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Since receiving the CAP’s recommendations, MSO has been working with partners to promote the proposed community norms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For example, a group of residents in Pioneer have come together through MSO’s Love Our ‘Hood Initiative to trial physical calendars at lift lobbies to be used by neighbours to inform one another in advance about potentially noisy activities, such as renovations and large gatherings at home.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: During these hours, excessive noise generating activities should be avoided.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Undoubtedly, this CAP recommendation reflects the views of those who suffer the ill effects of neighbourhood noise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: After all, those who are not affected by neighbourhood noise or those whose activities generate noise can hardly be expected to turn up at the CAP’s feedback sessions or fill in survey forms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: But it is important that CAP make this ask on behalf of Singaporeans who hope for more peace and quiet, and it is equally important that we find out whether the rest of Singapore is prepared to go along with it.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Anecdotally, some stakeholder groups have already begun ending their community events before 10.00 pm.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: So, some shifts have been happening on the ground.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: But for all of us to move together, we cannot overlook the impact that these extended hours, as recommended, could have on businesses and other community groups.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Thus, MSO is in the process of engaging the wider public and stakeholders to see how this can be adopted.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is part of our ForwardSG commitment to refresh our social compact to promote vibrant and peaceful neighbourhoods that all residents can enjoy living in.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To be meaningful, the decibel limit should cater to residential settings and not industrial or construction settings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To promote an understanding of the cause and effect of inter-floor noise disturbances, MSO will also be setting up an experiential space.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Inter-floor noise is a major category of neighbourhood noise feedback in our dense, high-rise environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Unfortunately, much of the feedback is subjective and speculative.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The feedback provider who suffers from noise can only describe its effect, and, often, after the fact.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Without the neighbour’s cooperation, it is hard to find out for sure whether and how the neighbour has caused the noise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: And as a community, we are none the wiser on exactly what transpired.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The experiential space will allow visitors to test first-hand how different actions create different decibel levels of noise and to challenge their perception on the direction of the noise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is a serious matter that the Government has been closely monitoring and studying.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: When the COVID-19 pandemic first hit in 2020, public feedback on neighbourhood noise, high-rise littering, smoking within homes and joss paper burning all saw significant increases.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will continue to monitor and review how various types of neighbour-related issues can be managed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For a start, our focus is on neighbourhood noise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: While most cases of noise disturbances can be improved through stronger community norms recommended by the CAP, Mr Henry Kwek is right in identifying the reality of a small set of severe cases where conflict between neighbours has become entrenched and acrimonious.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Often, there are signs that at least one of the conflicting parties purposely weaponise noise to cause suffering to their neighbours over a prolonged period.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We think this is wrong and strong actions are needed to put a stop to this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: MSO is a member of the interagency workgroup led by the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) that has been closely reviewing the Community Dispute Management Framework, or CDMF for short.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Minister Edwin Tong has shared how the powers and processes of the Community Disputes Resolution Tribunal, or CDRT, will be strengthened in his Ministry of Law (MinLaw) COS speech.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We hope this will provide faster and greater relief to residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In cases where noise is being used as a weapon to disrupt the peace among neighbours, we will include them under this new legal framework on mandatory mediation for community disputes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Minister Edwin Tong will elaborate further on the enhancements to move community disputes towards resolution during MCCY’s COS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The preferred mode of neighbourhood dispute resolution remains having both parties engage with each other.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: They will leverage stronger laws, such as mandating mediation under the enhanced CDMF, and actively work with affected parties to bring serious cases that are beyond self-help towards resolution.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: MSO has decided to host the pilot after careful consideration and after studying the experience of the Community Warden programme mentioned by Mr Yip Hon Weng and other efforts across the Government.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I know that many who have been long-suffering victims of neighbour-inflicted noise have pinned their hopes on Government intervention, which is all the more reason why I must highlight the following considerations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: First, this unit of dedicated personnel must not function as a first resort.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We do not wish to stunt the community’s capacity to resolve disputes early when they first occur.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: If people rely on Government personnel in the first instance to deal with their neighbours, it can only weaken our kampung spirit over time and we would all be the poorer for it.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Second, this unit is part of and not a substitute for an interlocking system of norm-setting, good neighbourly communication and the CDMF.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Having Government personnel stepping in to resolve differences between neighbours all the time is neither desirable nor sustainable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Third, this unit must, eventually, be vested with appropriate powers and use them sparingly but effectively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These include powers of investigation and powers to require nuisance makers to stop certain behaviours, pending mediation of the dispute.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: By making their presence felt at critical points of dispute resolution, we hope that this unit of dedicated personnel can deliver the right amount of intervention, bring relief to those who have a genuine grievance and discourage the wilful weaponisation of noise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We aim to stand up an initial team for this pilot by the end of the year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: (In Mandarin):   We recognise that Singaporeans are concerned about the rising cost of living.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is an issue that the Government is paying close attention to as well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: On this front, we are rolling out two measures targeted at helping our heartland shop owners and consumers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Second, the Government will require more coffeeshops to provide affordable food options for residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Since 2018, HDB has required new tenders of rental coffeeshops to provide six budget meals and a budget drink.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In addition, we want to tighten measures in managing neighbourhood disputes with a focus on managing neighbourhood noises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In the recent three years, the volume of neighbourhood noise cases has remained high.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In some cases, there are people who intentionally weaponise noise against their neighbours.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: MSO, MCCY and MinLaw will work together to strengthen various steps in the dispute resolution process.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In particular, MSO will pilot having a dedicated team to investigate and issue orders where necessary to facilitate the resolution of egregious noise-related disputes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I know that many who have been long-suffering victims of neighbour-inflicted noise have pinned their hopes on Government intervention, as they feel that communication and mediation cannot solve the problem.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Government is of the view that effective communication among neighbours remains the best way to maintain peace and harmony in the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: However, under certain circumstances, appropriate intervention from officials coupled with the proper use of mediation channels, can be effective.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: More details of the pilot will be announced when ready.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: (In English): I have shared how we will be enhancing our “hardware” and adjusting our “software” to build an endearing home for all.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: While we make progressive adjustments, we must remember our ideal – a gracious and accessible community for all Singaporeans to enjoy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Mr Chairman, the Built Environment sector is steadily recovering from COVID-19 and its associated disruptions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Manpower bottlenecks have eased, allowing contractors to catch up with delayed works.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: As of end-2022, the number of Construction Work Permit Holders have exceeded pre-COVID-19 levels.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Price increases for construction materials like concrete and steel rebars seem to be moderating.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Construction activities are almost back to pre-COVID-19 levels as well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Over the next few years, the projected construction demand is expected to be between $25 billion and $32 billion – remaining steady and stable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The public sector will be the main contributor as we ramp up BTO supply, build more hospitals and healthcare facilities and enhance our public transportation networks with projects like the Cross Island MRT line.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: There are many challenges and uncertainties ahead of us.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: That is why, even during COVID-19, we continued to push for sector transformation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Mr Chong Kee Hiong had asked about HDB’s efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: As the largest housing developer in Singapore, HDB plays a crucial leadership role in investing in innovation and promulgating good practices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: HDB has been implementing a range of technologies in the designing and building of new flats, like Building Information Modelling (BIM) and Design for Manufacturing and Assembly (DfMA).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Mr Chong will be pleased to note that, in fact, DfMA is used for all new HDB projects since 2021.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: In addition to Prefabricated Prefinished Volumetric Construction, or PPVC, HDB also adopts Advanced Precast Concrete System, or APCS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: APCS offers more opportunities for mechanisation and automation for large orders of prefabricated components.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: With these efforts, HDB has raised its site productivity by more than 25% compared to its 2010 levels.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: HDB is also investing in research and innovation to push the frontiers of construction productivity in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: For example, the flats will be built using a hybrid precast system made up of 3D and 2D components that are designed to be fabricated, transported and assembled more efficiently.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This system will also benefit residents, as it will enable HDB to build beamless flats with higher headroom and provide residents with greater flexibility in configuring the layout of their flats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: In addition to new builds, HDB has been exploring new ways to maintain public housing estates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: For instance, HDB is trialing a new concrete spalling prevention system, called the Corrosion Retardant System.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This forms a protective layer around the steel bars within the concrete to stop existing corrosion and prevent further spalling.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The trial results have been promising so far.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: HDB is studying how this system can address concrete spalling issues, especially in the older estates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Beyond HDB, we are partnering the industry on broader transformation efforts as part of the refreshed Build Environment Industry Transformation Map launched last September.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We are taking step to transform every part of the building life cycle – from the planning and design phase, the construction phase, to the operations and maintenance phase of our buildings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: One key enabler is digitalisation through the adoption of Integrated Digital Delivery or IDD.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This is a "digital spine" linking project stakeholders throughout the building lifecycle.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: As part of our IDD efforts, we developed the Common Data Environment or CDE, which is a data standards for the industry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This ensures data compatibility and allows for seamless digital collaboration between project stakeholders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: And we will continue to do more to support our SMEs in their digitalisation journey.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This scheme supports digital solutions that are tailored for the needs in the Build Environment sector and will complement the general digitalisation schemes that our SMEs can already tap on.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The solutions supported include 3D modelling and automation of quantity surveying and valuation tasks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Under this new tranche, the scheme will support manpower training so that SMEs can equip their employees with the necessary skills to make full use of these digital solutions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: One company that has benefited from this is United Force Engineering Pte Ltd, which tapped on the PSG to support the adoption of a Field Service Management software.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: I spoke to Ms Veni – the engineer behind the deployment of the solution at United Force Engineering.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Traditionally, tasks and payments were tracked manually on spreadsheets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: With the new software, Ms Veni and her team were able to automate several processes, like sending service reports to customers and tracking customer details.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: So, I invite firms to apply when the new tranche is available from April 2023.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: I agree with Mr Henry Kwek and Mr Yip Hon Weng that there are benefits to better upstream planning and coordination between industry stakeholders and the regulators.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We look forward to launching the digital platform that will implement this – CORENET X – by the end of this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Users will be onboarded in phases and features will be rolled out progressively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The platform will leverage BIM to enhance collaboration between industry stakeholders and between industry stakeholders and regulators on the various submissions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: It will also enable agencies to provide consolidated and coordinated responses to firms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: A large project typically takes about three to five years from design to building completion.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: To date, almost 500 consultant firms have participated in various engagements and sharing sessions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: So, I encourage the rest of the industry to find out more on the CORENET-X on our website.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This contains numerous resources, webinars and links to various community of practices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: I also encourage you to sign up for hands-on training courses that will be held throughout the year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Next, at the construction phase, we have been working to raise the adoption of DfMA technologies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The advantages were outlined by Mr Chong Kee Hiong earlier.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This involves shifting construction off-site to more factory-like settings before being assembled on site.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The benefits for such construction methods are numerous – there are productivity enhancements and better worker safety outcomes with fewer workers on-site.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This provides tax allowance for investments in advanced construction equipment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Over the last five years, the scheme has helped more than 60 firms make over $165 million worth of investments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: One such company is Sam Lain Equipment Services Pte Ltd, which tapped on this scheme to purchase a pipe jacking machine.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Sam Lain halved the time taken for pipe laying work and was able to reduce the number of site workers from 12 to seven.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: With less manual and temporary work involved and fewer workers onsite, they can now carry out this work more safely, with less disruption to the public.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Beyond deploying a single equipment to improve productivity for a specific task, Sam Lain has also invested in a suite of equipment, like silent piler machines and cranes to support different tasks related to underground and soil improvement works.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The minimum capital expenditure per equipment will remain at $100,000.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: I encourage all firms to consider applying for the IAS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Proper maintenance ensures that a development is safe, functional and enjoyable for its users and greatly reduces energy emissions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: At the same time, the maintenance costs of a building over its lifetime can be around three to four times that of the initial construction costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: There is hence a need to manage these costs more effectively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The Government will do more to champion transformation in the FM industry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: First, the public sector will take the lead for the buildings under our care.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We require all new public sector developments, existing public sector buildings undergoing retrofitting works and developments on Government Land Sales sites to adopt best practices in designing for maintainability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This will reduce the workload of FM firms downstream.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: BCA is also working with agencies to drive greater adoption of Integrated Facilities Management, or IFM, and Aggregated Facilities Management, or AFM in their buildings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We will continue support the industry in this effort.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We launched a $30 million grant last September to support the adoption of progressive FM procurement, processes and technologies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: To date, about 20 companies have expressed interest and I encourage more firms to apply.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: I am very glad to see that many industry partners are also playing their part.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The Singapore International Facility Management Association, or SIFMA, and the Trade Associations and Chambers of other FM related sectors, like Security and Landscaping have stepped up to explore potential collaboration projects to improve integration across the various FM disciplines.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: I commend them for their effort and look forward to partnering them to transform our FM sector including promulgating good practices like outcome-based contracting.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: In particular, we are stepping up efforts for buildings, which account for over 20% of Singapore's carbon emissions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: I agree with Mr Xie Yao Quan, Ms Tin Pei Ling, Mr Don Wee and Mr Cheng Hsing Yao that we need to operate and maintain buildings more sustainably.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: But collectively, we must intensify our greening efforts, to reach our national target of achieving net-zero emissions by 2050.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: In particular, we need to do more to green our existing stock of older buildings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: These buildings may not have been designed with sustainability in mind or may not be operated or maintained efficiently.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: And this can result in significant energy wastage, sometimes more than a quarter of the buildings' overall energy use.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Currently, BCA requires buildings that undergo major works or chiller retrofits to meet minimum energy performance requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This ensures that older buildings are upgraded to meet prevailing sustainability standards when they undertake extensive works.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: These buildings will be required to maintain an improved level of energy performance over a stipulated period.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: These measures can include simple, cost-effective solutions, such as replacing faulty parts and sensors, or getting tenants to use energy saving lighting.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Building owners who would like to undertake more extensive retrofits can also apply for grants under the Green Mark Incentive Scheme for Existing Buildings 2.0, which provides up to 50% co-funding for retrofitting works to achieve at least Green Mark Platinum standards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: BCA is consulting relevant stakeholders, including building owners, developers, energy auditors and professional associations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: These stakeholders recognise the need for this regime as most buildings would unlikely undergo works to reduce energy consumption if such works were not made mandatory.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: BCA will continue to engage the industry on the implementation details.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: There will inevitably be extenuating circumstances or practical constraints for certain buildings to meet the requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: And BCA will take this feedback into consideration.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: BCA will assure that building owners are notified early and have sufficient time to comply with the requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: In the meantime, building owners who would like to know how the energy performance of their buildings compares to others can refer to BCA's building energy benchmarking report.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Currently, this annual report provides a summary of the energy performance for each building typology and the individual energy performance data for commercial buildings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Starting this year, BCA will also provide individual energy performance data for healthcare facilities, sports and recreation centres and institutional buildings and identify them by name.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Buildings will be ranked by energy performance amongst other buildings of similar typology.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The next edition of the report will be published later this month on BCA's website.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: I encourage all building owners to study it and use it as a guide to improve your building's energy performance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Our efforts to transform into a world-class Built Environment (BE) sector will also create exciting job opportunities for our BE professionals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: For instance, the push towards digitalisation and DfMA will change the nature of work in our sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The push towards greater sustainability will also mean greater demand for green professionals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This is something Mr Xie Yao Quan mentioned too.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: And exciting new roles include energy and sustainability solutions architects, specialists in design for maintainability, solar engineers, facility management data analysts and many more exciting opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: So, I encourage all BE professionals to upskill and reskill yourselves so you can take full advantage of the new opportunities in the BE sector, both locally and abroad.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: BCA has been engaging industry stakeholders on how to prepare their workforce for the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We will also consider all suggestions on how to improve HR practices, as suggested by various Members earlier.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Mr Chairman, I provided an update on the various transformation efforts across the building lifecycle.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: However, fundamental transformation of an industry sector is not just about using technology or improving work processes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Crucially, there is also a need to transform mindsets and culture – aspects which are often harder to do.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: At the most basic level, we must make sure that hygiene factors are met.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This includes timely payment, as raised by Mr Yip Hon Weng.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: In this regard, the Security of Payment Act, or SOPA has served to enable regular payments in the construction sector since 2005.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The Public Sector Standard Conditions of Contracts (PSSCOC) also stipulates payment timeframes that all public agencies are required to abide by.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: But contractors can also do their part by providing the necessary documents in a timely manner, to facilitate evaluation and approval of payments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: If there are specific project issues encountered by Mr Yip, BCA will be happy to follow up with the Member separately.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: However, I believe most industry stakeholders would very much prefer to resolve issues amicably rather than going to mediation or adjudication or even legal action.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: A promising approach to promote a more positive work culture is collaborative contracting.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
