text: Collaborative contracting aligns the interests of all project parties towards shared project goals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This facilitates proactive project management and prompt resolution of claims before they escalate into major disputes or costs and can help tackle this issue of timely payment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We have seen encouraging successes in other jurisdictions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The Government is taking the lead to adopt collaborative contracting.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: There are at least 10 public sector projects that have piloted or will be piloting collaborative contracting.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: But we also need the private sector on board.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This will be amongst the first in Singapore for the private sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: They have committed to sharing its experiences with the wider industry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: BCA will work with them to develop standard collaborative contracting provisions, which the industry can then later reference and adopt.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: CapitaLand and its partners, including Woh Hup and Threesixty, will try out new contract provisions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This includes provisions that enable project parties to flag problems, like design deviations early and provide incentives for better performance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: To resolve disputes in a more structured manner, the alliance also intends to establish a dispute resolution board, comprising senior management of key stakeholders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Taken together, these will better facilitate the smooth and timely delivery of projects, benefiting not just project parties, but the eventual building users too.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The idea is for these groups of firms to collaborate on multiple projects over time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: In doing so, they can grow deeper capabilities and develop innovative approaches that can eventually benefit the entire ecosystem.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Another alliance under the GTS is led by UOL.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: UOL and its partners, including United Tec, will focus on developing new capabilities to enhance construction productivity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: To increase automation, the alliance plans to adopt robots for labour-intensive tasks, such as cleaning and installing building components.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This can reduce required manpower by up to 40%.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: For example, one of the identified solutions is a lift installation robot.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This will not only reduce safety risks for workers but will also ensure consistent workmanship and quality across all installation works.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: It will also adopt more advanced prefabrication techniques and technologies and prefabricate more components, such as Mechanical and Electrical systems.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This is expected to reduce the manpower required for such activities by up to 45% and minimise future disruptions to the alliance's supply chain.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: I commend CapitaLand, UOL and their respective partners on leading the way.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Their commitment to working together will not only help uplift their respective value chains, but also push the boundaries for the rest of the sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: (In Mandarin):   Although our Built Environment (BE) sector faces headwinds, it is recovering steadily.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Manpower shortages have eased and construction material costs have largely stabilised.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Projected construction demand over the next few years will remain stable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Most of the demand will come from the public sector, including the construction of new HDB flats, healthcare facilities, the Cross Island MRT Line and Changi Airport T5 Terminal.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Going forward, we must continue to work together to further transform the BE sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: First, we will launch the CORENET X electronic platform by the end of this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This new platform will simplify the process of submitting building plans to regulators and reduce the time taken to obtain approvals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: SMEs will be provided with funding support of up to 50% of qualifying costs when adopting pre-approved digital solutions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Businesses can enjoy tax allowances when they invest in advanced construction equipment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We have shaken off the shadow of the pandemic and can finally see the light at the end of the tunnel.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The Government will continue to work together with the industry to make our BE sector more resilient and sustainable, as well as continue efforts to improve its productivity and reduce its reliance on manual labour.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: (In English): Let me now turn to another important topic of interest to Members here.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Everyone has a role to play in ensuring safe and positive human-wildlife encounters.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: As individuals, we must learn how to share spaces with our wildlife.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: For example, we can observe from a distance when we come across animals and avoid intruding into their spaces.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: It may trigger a reaction from animals, especially mothers protecting the young.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We can also refrain from feeding wildlife as this can alter their natural foraging behaviour and lead to increases in their population.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Community partners can help to jointly develop and implement solutions for wildlife management.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: I am glad that we have the support of partners like the Urban Wildlife Working Group (UWG) and Otter Working Group in this regard.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The Otter Working Group closely follows the otter families and their movements and shares this information with NParks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This allows NParks to proactively cordon off areas with young otter pups to minimise the likelihood of human-wildlife conflict.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: NParks implements a holistic suite of measures to manage the wildlife population, including habitat modification and food source reduction.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: NParks works with NEA and SFA on many of these efforts, such as reducing food sources for pest birds at food establishments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Where necessary to protect public safety, NParks also undertakes population control measures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: NParks monitors bird feeding hotspots and works with Town Councils and NEA to carry out targeted enforcement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We will continue to educate members of the community through platforms, such as school assembly talks, public webinars and HDB's MyNiceHome roadshows.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: These efforts are supported by science, through population surveys and research studies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: These help us better understand the ecology of our wildlife, so that we can continue to refine our approach.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Mr Chong Kee Hiong also raised specific pest bird and chicken-related issues in the estates in his constituency.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: As a fellow Member of Parliament, I fully empathise with Mr Chong on his current situation – caught between different communities of his residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Recently, we had an extended discussion during Question Time where we spoke about this issue of chickens and cocks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: In fact, this was because of the cut raised by Mr Ang Wei Neng, Mr Louis Ng jumped in, and I think Assoc Prof Jamus Lim from Sengkang also raised an intractable Town Council issue of persistent crowing, which we managed to solve with him.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: I offered some tips to Assoc Prof Jamus Lim at that point of time on how to deal with crowing cocks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: I will be happy to share those tips with Mr Chong separately.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: But I would like to assure Mr Chong that NParks is aware of and will continue to support the Town Council and his grassroots leaders in tackling these issues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: In addition to promoting safe and responsible human-wildlife encounters, we must also protect animal health and welfare.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Mr Louis Ng and Mr Leon Perera have asked about our approach to managing animal abuse and cruelty, specifically on whether we will consider raising penalties for such offences.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Again, we had a recent discussion in this House on this topic in response to a Parliamentary Question raised by Mr Louis Ng.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: NParks investigates all feedback on such cases and takes the appropriate enforcement action.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: In cases where individuals suffer from psychiatric conditions, the Courts may already direct a Mandatory Treatment Order.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: So, it is part of the regime today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We will consult the public and relevant stakeholders on our proposals and will share more details when available.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: To Mr Louis Ng's question, we are looking to further promote the well-being of pet and community cats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We are in the midst of a public consultation on the proposed cat management framework.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This framework aims to promote responsible cat ownership and caregiving, while safeguarding public health.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Alongside this, we will study allowing pet cats in HDB flats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We are conducting a detailed analysis of the results and will share our findings when ready.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: So, I can assure Mr Louis Ng that we are not pussy-footing around this issue and this is certainly not a cat-and-mouse game as he mentioned earlier.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Lastly, Mr Leon Perera also provided some suggestions on how we can enhance efforts in tackling the global illegal wildlife trade, such as working with other countries and the local community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: As the Member has said, we had an extensive debate on this topic when we moved the amendments to the Endangered Species (Import and Export) Act last year and I am glad that the Member supported the Government's approach on the amendments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: But let me briefly reiterate a few points.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: In fact, our efforts have been recognised internationally.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: I am glad that the Member also agrees with us that global action and international cooperation are key.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Many cases of illegal wildlife trade involve entities in multiple countries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: In the debate to move the amendments last year, Mr Leon Perera asked if Singapore should consider a different approach to regulating wildlife trade, to use a reverse listing model, which will make "no trade" the default.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: So, it is important that our approach to illegal wildlife trade is aligned with CITES regulations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: At the local level, we will continue to engage various stakeholders, including TCM shops and the community, to raise awareness on the role that they can play in combating illegal wildlife trade.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: In closing, I would like to reiterate our commitment to engaging community and industry partners across a range of issues, from the Built Environment sector transformation to navigating human-wildlife interactions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Together, I am confident that we will be able to adapt and evolve our approaches to tackle emerging challenges that may come our way.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Moving from wildlife, chickens and cats, Minister of State Faishal Ibrahim.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In my speech, I will share more about how the MND family is building an inclusive and caring home for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I will focus on three main areas: firstly, empowering lower-income households by pairing housing with social support; secondly, taking care of the housing needs of seniors; and thirdly, partnering the community to create vibrant and endearing places.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Recognising that they start off with less, we have designed our system to provide more help to them, for example, through housing schemes and grants that are tiered by income, so that, with a stable job, they, too, can buy a home of their own.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As a result, Singapore’s home ownership rate is one of the highest in the world, including for our lower-income households.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: At the same time, some families may not be ready for home ownership yet, because they need to build up and stabilise their finances first.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For low-income households who do not have other housing options, our Public Rental Scheme (PRS) serves as a social safety net – providing these households a safe space and a stable base, where they can build up their stability and self-reliance and, eventually, buy their own flat.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The rents are highly-subsidised to ensure that they are affordable.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As we have shared before, we assess all requests for public rental flats holistically, considering all relevant factors, including applicants’ household size, family support, housing budget and housing options.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For those who have no other housing options, we will assist them with a public rental flat.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Due to COVID-19, we saw higher demand in 2020 and 2021.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The severe labour crunch in the construction industry also disrupted how quickly HDB could build new flats and spruce up vacated ones before renting them out to new tenants.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: To overcome these sprucing delays, HDB worked closely with its contractors and brought in new ones.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: HDB streamlined the customer journey for rental applicants to allow them to select from available flats across Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This alleviated the longer waiting time in certain regions.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For applicants who are in urgent need of a rental flat, HDB will prioritise allocating a flat to them.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will continue to monitor the demand closely, given potential economic headwinds, and we are studying options to augment the supply.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We have also been improving the living environment for our tenants and ensuring that our HDB neighbourhoods are inclusive.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Our newer rental blocks and flats have better design, lighting and ventilation.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We have also been building rental flats with sold flats in the same BTO projects and, where possible, we build rental flats in the same block as sold flats.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Murali Pillai and Ms Sylvia Lim spoke about tackling overcrowding in public rental flats and providing larger flats to large families with young children.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We understand these concerns and we want to help parents to provide a better home environment for their children.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For all families staying in public rental, our goal is to uplift them, so that they can buy their own flat eventually.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: That is why we provide significant support to help families to own a home.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: While they build up their finances, we do our best to take care of their housing needs, through public rental.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Families with at least three members can be allocated to a 2-room public rental flat.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Those that form two family nuclei, such as families with children, parents and grandparents living together, can apply for another flat.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will offer them a second flat in the same block where possible.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Some families staying in public rental flats face complex and interlocking challenges, which make it difficult for them to progress to home ownership.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: So, we are going upstream to provide support in a holistic way that addresses each family’s unique set of needs and aspirations.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Once a family applies for a public rental flat from HDB and is assessed to be eligible, the family will be automatically enrolled in ComLink.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: A ComLink officer will contact the family to understand their situation and connect them with relevant assistance, even before they move into their flat.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: After the family moves into their rental flat, a ComLink officer will continue to journey with the family, regularly check in on how they are doing, and coordinate support from Government and community partners.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: By providing coordinated support early, right from the time that families enter rental housing, we believe that we can support more families to achieve stability, self-reliance and, ultimately, social mobility.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: MSF will share more about ComLink at their COS.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: When families have built up their finances with stable employment and income, they can count on our full support to buy a flat of their own.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For example, they can receive one-to-one guidance through their home-buying journey from HDB’s Home ownership Support Team (HST).

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Over the past three years, HST has reached out to about 1,400 households.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: One family who has moved into their new home is Mdm Nurul and Mr Rozi.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: After getting married, the couple stayed together in public rental housing for about 11 years.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As the family grew in size, they moved from a 1-room flat to a 2-room flat.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As their children grew older, the couple set themselves the goal of buying their own home to provide more space for the family.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Rozi worked as a cleaner while Mdm Nurul took care of the family.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: When they received HST's outreach SMS in 2020, they contacted HST.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Our HST officer guided the couple to understand their housing budget and options, and the support available.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: With that knowledge, the couple applied for a 3-room balance flat at Ang Mo Kio, to be nearer to their child's school.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: With a stable job and income, they were able to qualify for the Enhanced CPF Housing Grant and an HDB housing loan.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: They moved into their flat in October 2021, and they are happy to have their own home.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Some families had to move into public rental housing after losing their flat due to financial difficulties or other life events.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We hope the enhancements will encourage more families to work towards buying their own home.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We are happy for every one of them.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Their success stories show that home ownership is achievable for families staying in public rental housing, with hard work and commitment on their part, coupled with strong support from the Government and the community.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We have also been making improvements to public rental housing for low-income single tenants, who rent under the Joint Singles Scheme (JSS).

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: While many of them can find a flatmate and live together amicably, we know that some find it difficult.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We have been working on addressing concerns about the JSS, while managing within our land and resource constraints.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Since 2015, we have been building new rental flats with high partitions, to provide more privacy for tenants in their sleeping areas.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We have also been installing partitions in existing flats at tenants' request since 2019.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: There are now about 1,300 flats with partitions.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In 2021, we started piloting the JSS Operator-Run model (JSS-OR).

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For each JSS-OR site, HDB appoints a social service agency to manage and mediate the flat-sharing arrangements and provide social support for tenants.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Several Members have asked for an update on the pilot.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We currently have three JSS-OR sites – in Bedok, Buangkok and Bukit Batok – which can accommodate around 400 tenants in total.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The pilot has been well-subscribed, and all three sites are close to full occupancy.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The feedback from our tenants has been positive, and they appreciate having the operator on-site.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: While some differences between co-tenants are inevitable, most can be resolved through early mediation by the operator, which prevents disagreements from escalating.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The operators also conduct regular check-ins with the tenants and organise social activities for them.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: One JSS-OR tenant is Mdm Chan, who is 75 years old and stays in a 1-room flat at Bukit Batok with her flat mate.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: They share a good bond and often help each other out.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For example, Mdm Chan, who is bilingual, helps to translate letters and conversations in English for her Mandarin-speaking flatmate.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: She enjoys cooking and shares her home-cooked food with her neighbours.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: She also participates in social activities and celebrations organised by the operator – New Hope Community Services.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: When my colleagues met Mdm Chan recently, she shared with them that she was happy to be staying there.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The three sites at Bukit Panjang, Bidadari and Sengkang will be able to accommodate 600 tenants in total.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We expect to open the new sites for application by the end of this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will continue to learn from this pilot and find more ways to improve the lives of singles in public rental.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Some face housing difficulties due to unexpected and unfortunate life events, such as divorce.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Lim Biow Chuan and Mr Murali Pillai spoke about some of these difficulties.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We have been adjusting our policies over the years to take care of their housing needs and smoothen the housing transition for them.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We want to ensure that they have a stable home, especially for their children.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Divorcees with children can buy a subsidised flat from HDB or a resale flat on the open market and qualify for the same housing schemes and grants as other families.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Those who are buying a flat as second-timers can receive priority under the ASSIST scheme when they apply for a 2-room Flexi or 3-room BTO flat in non-mature estates.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Those who require interim accommodation while waiting for their BTO flats to be completed can apply to rent a flat under the Parenthood Provisional Housing Scheme.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For divorcees who cannot afford to buy a subsidised flat and do not have other housing options or family support, HDB will assist them with public rental housing.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Those in very urgent need of housing can also seek help from MSF's shelters while applying for a public rental flat.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We understand that divorcing parties want assurance on their next housing arrangement.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: These matters have to be resolved as they affect the parties' eligibility to purchase a flat.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For those who need more time to sell their flat due to special circumstances, HDB will assess each request based on its merits.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Murali Pillai spoke about ensuring that the housing needs of the children are addressed when the Court decides on the division of the matrimonial flat.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: When deciding the division of the matrimonial flat, the Court does consider the welfare and needs of the children and may consider HDB's input.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For example, HDB will provide information to the Court on the matrimonial flat and post-divorce housing options for the divorcing parties and their children when asked by the Court.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The Court can also refer divorcing parents to HDB for housing counselling before the divorce is finalised, for them to better understand their post-divorce housing options.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will continue to work with the Court to find ways to improve these processes, to ensure that the housing needs of the children are taken care of.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We want to ensure that our HDB flats and towns support our seniors to live long, healthy and happy lives, within the communities they are familiar with.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We have been planning ahead and making our homes and towns more inclusive for seniors over the years.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For example, we introduced the Enhancement for Active Seniors (EASE) programme in 2012.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We have also been adding senior-friendly features, such as elderly fitness equipment, residents' corners and community gardens, to our HDB estates, as part our neighbourhood upgrading programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: More recently, together with MOH, we introduced Community Care Apartments (CCAs) – a new housing typology that pairs senior-friendly housing with care services.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: It will offer about 200 units, alongside other flat types in the development.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Residents will be able to conveniently access fitness stations, a playground and community gardens.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: These amenities encourage active ageing and provide opportunities for residents of different ages to interact.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The site will also be located near Active Ageing Centres, community centres, markets and hawker centres.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We are also partnering the private sector to co-create innovative assisted living models that can cater to seniors' diverse preferences and lifestyles.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In collaboration with MOH, URA launched a pilot private assisted-living site at Parry Avenue for sale in September last year.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The tender is closing later this month, and we look forward to receiving novel proposals.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For seniors who want to tap on their flat to supplement their retirement income, we offer a range of monetisation options.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Those who wish to continue living in their homes can take up the Lease Buyback Scheme (LBS) or rent out spare bedrooms.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For those who want to right-size, we offer 2-room Flexi flats and the Silver Housing Bonus (SHB).

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will continue reaching out to seniors, through local community events, public talks and the media, to share about these housing monetisation options.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Together with MOH and other agencies, we will also continue to meet the housing and care needs of our seniors and support them to stay healthy and engaged within the community.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will share more details of our plans later this year as part of Forward Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We would like to thank all Members for all their suggestions.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: One example is the public engagement exercise conducted by Kampong Gelam Alliance (KGA) to shape the place plan for Kampong Gelam Historic Area.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Miss Cheryl Chan and Ms Nadia Samdin asked about the Kampong Gelam Historic Area.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In total, we have engaged more than 1,600 stakeholders, such as local businesses and community groups, as well as members of the public, through workshops and online surveys.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Many of them shared that it is important to continue supporting traditional trades while attracting new ones to the precinct.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: There is also strong support for initiatives to showcase the precinct's rich history and culture and recognition of the need for strong local partnerships among stakeholders.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: KGA and URA will study these findings carefully and incorporate suggestions into the final place plan.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This will complement several other projects that have been piloted at Kampong Gelam, such as a recent citizen engagement project by NHB and URA, to document the stories of heritage businesses.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: These collective efforts will keep the Kampong Gelam Historic Area thriving as a centre of community, culture and enterprise.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: (In Malay):   In his speech, Minister Desmond Lee provided an update on the further efforts that we will make to take care of the housing needs of different segments of Singaporeans, from those buying their first home to seniors in their golden years.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: To support couples buying their first home, we already set aside the vast majority of the BTO flat supply for first-timer families – at least 95% of the 4-room flats, in both mature and non-mature estates.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Last year, we arranged several sessions of the Forward Singapore Housing Conversations, where there was a strong consensus to give more help to young married couples and families buying their first home.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: To qualify for this category, they must also not have owned or sold any residential property nor had the chance to book a flat in the past five years.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will help them to get a flat more quickly in three ways.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: To reflect this expansion, we will rename it as the Family and Parenthood Priority Scheme.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Third, for BTO flats in non-mature estates, we will give first priority to First-Timer Parents and Married Couples for the flats set aside under the Family and Parenthood Priority Scheme, if they apply for a 4-room or smaller flat.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This means that they will be shortlisted ahead of all other applicants eligible for the scheme, and thus, stand a higher chance of being invited to select a flat.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We also take care of families that may not be ready for home ownership yet, because they need to stabilise their finances first.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For low-income households with no other housing options, our public rental flats offer them shelter, a safe space, and a stable base where they can build up stability and self-reliance.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For families staying in public rental flats, our goal is to uplift their lives, so that they can eventually buy a flat of their own.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This is achieved by providing holistic support much earlier, to help them address the multiple and interlocking challenges that they face.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The Community Link Rental Scheme, which we launched together with Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) in November last year, pairs rental housing with holistic support for families with children, right from the start.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Once a family applies for a public rental flat from HDB and is assessed to be eligible, the family will be automatically enrolled in ComLink.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: A ComLink officer will contact the family to understand their situation and connect them with relevant assistance, even before they move into their rental flat.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: After the family moves into their rental flat, an officer will continue to journey with the family, regularly check in on how they are doing, and coordinate support from Government and community partners.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: By providing them with coordinated support right from the point of entry to rental housing, we believe we can help more families achieve stability, self-reliance, and ultimately social mobility, including home ownership.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: When families have built up their finances with stable employment and income, they can count on our full support to buy a flat of their own.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We have also been making improvements to the public rental Joint Singles Scheme, or JSS.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We started piloting the Joint Singles Scheme - Operator-Run (JSS-OR) model in 2021.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For each JSS-OR site, HDB appoints a social service agency to manage the flat-sharing arrangements, provide social support to tenants, and mediate amongst tenants when needed.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We currently have three sites, which can accommodate around 400 tenants.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: These three sites, which will be at Bukit Panjang, Bidadari, and Sengkang, can accommodate a total of about 600 tenants.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We expect to open applications for these three sites later this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: (In English): Madam, let me reaffirm our commitment to build an inclusive home for all Singaporeans – where home ownership remains affordable and accessible, including for low-income Singaporeans; where we integrate housing with social support to empower and uplift our lower-income households; where our homes and towns support the needs of our seniors; and where we partner the community to create vibrant and endearing places.

speaker: The Chairman
text: We have time for questions, I see quite a lot of hands going up.

speaker: The Chairman
text: So, I am going to ask that Members be succinct with your questions and two clarifications for each of you.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: I have got two questions for Minister Desmond Lee.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: The first is, with the inclusion of the first-timer, the parents and the married couples in the Family and Parenthood Priority Scheme, will this impact or affect those who are already today eligible for the PPS scheme?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: The second one is with the first-timer families, because they are those who have disposed of their private property or even a non-subsidised HDB flat, they because of financial reasons will have a need to go for subsidised flat now.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: So, what is the rationale for only prioritising the first-timers or those who we think have never owned or sold any local residential property before?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We are in a situation where demand is high for the various reasons that we have articulated during the Housing Motion.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have ramped up supply but we hear from the various Housing Conversations under Forward Singapore that there is a group of Singaporeans who are undertaking their very first home ownership journey: younger people who have just graduated who just started work looking for their very first home.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: While they are first-timers, people think that they should get extra help to get their very first home.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Hence, we have scoped the group that will get this extra support and they will be a sub-category within the first-timer group.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: On the second question, why did we scope the First-Timer Parent and Married Couple subcategory to exclude those who had formerly owned or sold property.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is to enable us to achieve our aim of giving additional support to those who are buying their very first home.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This would tend to be younger people who are just starting out, they may not have worked long enough to accumulate the resources or gain the incomes that older, more experienced Singaporeans have in getting more housing options.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And so, helping them in this way allows them to get their very first home.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, those who had previously bought and sold properties would probably have more means.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But I hear the Member that they may be extenuating circumstances and I did say that HDB will look at families in extenuating circumstances.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Be that as it may, they would still be considered first-timers, like everyone else in that category.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Earlier in his speech, he mentioned that there is no household income ceiling as such but the application will be assessed holistically.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: However, if you were to look at the HDB website today, there is still a mention of this $1,500 household income as most applicants fulfilling this criterion.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, I have two questions relating to this.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: First, why is the $1,500 figure still mentioned on the website?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: And secondly, in our experience residents have been turned away from the scheme because their income exceeded that threshold.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, could he share some information with us about the flexibility HDB has exercised?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: For example, how many households have they approved to go onto the public rental scheme that have exceeded this income ceiling, or some other data for us to understand the flexibility aspect better?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, it is not one but a fair bit of percentage.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Essentially, we look at it from a holistic point of view: the household size, the background and whether they have any housing options and so forth.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The amount that we shared on the website that Member referred to, let me read, it states here.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Applications are reviewed holistically taking into account household size and individual circumstances." And that is what we have done.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We say that most of our applicants have a household income of below $1,500, and if yours is above this, you can still submit an application and we will evaluate your eligibility accordingly.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I work very closely with my colleagues in the rental section and this is something that we have been helping fellow Singaporeans on.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: She announced today that MSO will pilot having a dedicated team members to address egregious cases of neighbourhood noise.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: There are existing efforts such as those by the grassroots and Community Mediation Centre.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: How does this proposed pilot enhance the current framework for community mediation and for disputes, and how does it complement the existing efforts by grassroots, MCCY and MinLaw?

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We have every intention for this unit of dedicated personnel, when it is piloted, to work with the existing officers, for instance, from HDB, who have been handling such cases from time to time and also the grassroots, to help to bring cases to resolution.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: The difference in this case would be that the dedicated personnel would be able, we hope, for instance, to be on site to corroborate reports that there have been noises at certain times, to verify whether that is, in fact, true.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We hope to exercise some investigative powers because, today, quite a lot of what the grassroots as well as what some Government agencies' officers are able to do, they cannot get very far if there is no consent given by the person who is suspected of making noise.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Of course, today, there are also no powers to ask the person to cease and desist from making noise, pending satisfactory mediation or otherwise resolution of the case.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: So, that, I think, would be the difference.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: MND and HDB have committed to building faster and building more.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It will require the building capacity of our built environment sector.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: My colleague Senior Minister of State Tan Kiat How has spoken earlier about the productivity and innovation journey that HDB had brought onboard in order for us to undertake a building of this scale.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Members would also recognise that the flats that we are building today are much taller, more comprehensive, have more amenities and facilities than the flats of yesteryear.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: At the scale that we are undertaking, it requires resources, it requires manpower, it requires land.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But we are committed to persisting with this ramp-up in order to meet the demand for housing by Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: I have just two related clarifications on open market rental affordability.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And for those who have urgent housing needs, with Interim Rental Housing (IRH) flats as well.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As I said earlier, with the large number of flats as well as private properties completing this year and over the next two years, we think that that may have some impact on the overall rental market.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But we, certainly keep an open mind and keep a close eye on the rental situation and will be prepared to take necessary measures in order to support Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: I wanted to follow up on my question or suggestion, in order to unlock the resale market, whether those who are buying private property can be asked to sell their flats or be barred from renting their HDB flat.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As I have said previously in response to some Parliamentary Questions, we are studying this issue.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It is a small group, but we will continue to study whether it is necessary and appropriate to prevent HDB home owners who have bought private property from renting out their HDB flats.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: One is that as we push for more flexible work arrangements, including work-from-home, I am wondering whether MND is looking at how we can enhance or redesign the living environment to better enable this, because one of the feedback is that, sometimes, there is not enough space or it is too noisy for that.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: How are we going to develop or redevelop those while taking into consideration that some of these sites actually do have emotional attachments that people will have towards them like homes, like flats?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As I have shared previously, we are looking at the possibility of HDB housing design where we have more open plan flexibilities for the owner.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Already, we have pushed the structural elements of each flat as far as possible to the outer perimeter of the flat.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, you try to avoid having structural beams and columns within the flat, which make it difficult for the homeowner to adjust the interior of the flat.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And this will not just impact our design of the interior of the flat but also causing us to think about the design of future housing estates, that is, not just the flat but the neighbourhood as well as future town centres and neighbourhood centres.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But, already, as the Member may have noticed in the media, we are experimenting with different things, even putting work modules that some companies are piloting at the bottom of the flats in the void decks, with WiFi and other facilities to see whether that is something that Singaporeans take to.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Libraries as well as CCs have during COVID-19 and some continued well after the COVID-19 pandemic to offer such spaces for Singaporeans to work away from office.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And, of course, there are the private sector co-working spaces that are found in different parts of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And we are studying with them the kinds of subscription to these kinds of models.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: She has identified something where we need to maintain a balance.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And in the early days, where it was largely just greenfield, it was not an issue.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But now, we find that that is becoming increasingly scarce and we have to try and make sure that we preserve green spaces.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But at the same time, there is a need for development.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, we have got to balance the two.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: They are exciting because it gives you an opportunity to redevelop and build on something which exists.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And the big thing now for anybody who is in the infrastructure space is how do you take something which is an existing building and make it sustainable.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And there are a lot of technologies and solutions that are going into this so that you actually turn something which is brown green again.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Then, you may also have to tear down something which is existing and build afresh on it, redevelop it.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And when you do that, that is when I think some of us, depending on the building, its location and what it was associated with, then you may lose some of the heritage and that cultural association.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, we have to have a good balance and we assess the buildings and the site.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And if there is a heritage value, then we have to see whether you preserve the whole thing or whether you might have to redevelop it but you preserve some parts of it, for example, the old Police Academy where we are going to have residential buildings.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But we did not want to raze it completely.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We also spoke to the old Police officers who had gone through the Police Academy.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And there will be a part of it which will be retained there.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And if you look at the URA long-term plan review, there was a segment which was the Paya Lebar Air Base, we can see how, this is still at the concept stage, but they tried very hard to make sure that parts of the runway would still be there so as to preserve that association.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, if I had to sum it up, I would say that our approach is really heart, home and heritage.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: I understand I spoke very quickly given the nature of a 30-second cut, albeit not as fast as some other Members are able to.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: I had suggested that one alternative use of the MSCP beyond bicycle parking was temporary parking for delivery riders.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: I think I am not alone in experiencing delivery riders that are illegally parking along HDB service roads.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: So, I am wondering if the case-by-case consideration for MSCP ground floor repurposing will extend to such uses.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: The second clarification is for Senior Minister of State Sim Ann.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: I appreciate that there are many contributors to the cost of food, including raw ingredients as well as labour.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: But this should actually apply nationwide, whereas what I had compared, in terms of the significant price differential, was between mature and non-mature estates.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: So, I reiterate my call to explore alternative option mechanisms for new HDB coffee shops and I am wondering if that is something that you would consider.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The alternative uses would have to be assessed on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, I think not every multi-storey car park, for example, would need temporary parking for delivery riders.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But if there is a need for it, and if the precinct assesses that this is something that they require, they are always free to put up the proposal to HDB.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: And that is a dialogue that I believe will be a fruitful one.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: By and large, in terms of coffee shop pricing, it is not in the interest of operators to price themselves out of the reach of their consumers.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We also understand that in different precincts, there may be some variations, but the important thing, and I believe the Member also shares his concern, is that the resultant price to the consumers, there should be affordable options.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: I believe that our approach would cover both the leased coffee shops, and also, we will start that conversation with the sold coffee shops.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I just wanted to add to my response to Assoc Prof Jamus Lim, which is that the suggestion of having space for delivery drivers is being piloted in some areas.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The designated lots provide the delivery personnel with space, to sort and to handle the parcels.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, there is these two ongoing pilots which we are studying as well.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: I just have two questions for Senior Minister of State Tan, and I promise they are not on chickens and cats.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: First, on the construction industry, I am glad to hear Senior Minister of State Tan's update that HDB is playing a leading role in driving the demand for productive construction practices to help the industry transform, but the rest of the public sector is also a major developer of buildings and infrastructure, and there are very significant construction budgets.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: So, I would just like to ask: how might MND help to corral the whole-of-public service and galvanise the whole-of-public sector to drive the demand for productive construction practices in the industry.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: The second question on the Built Environment (BE), in terms of the sustainable solutions that the BE sector is going to generate in the years ahead, be it in construction development or maintenance, what might be MND's plans to help our companies to export these capabilities and generate economic value in the years to come for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: On the first one, BCA is taking the lead to bring together the various Government agencies who are in the infrastructure space.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: For example, the Land Transport Authority (LTA), JTC Corporation (JTC) for industrial properties and so on.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: They are known as the Government Procuring Entities, or GPEs for short.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: BCA is taking the lead to bring them together.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Collectively, we are trying to raise productivity and transform the BE sector.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: I just mentioned a few things that might be noteworthy for the Member.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: I spoke about the collaborative contracting model earlier.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: This is a very important approach that raises the level of productivity and encourages a shared alignment of project stakeholders' interests towards common project goals so that issues are resolved early, tackling issues early.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Hopefully, this would lead to reduced cost and reduce time delays as much as possible.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So, that is one, at the contracting stage, we are looking how to implement good practices like collaborative contracting.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: The second is to support Singapore's transition towards a green economy under the GreenGov.SG programme.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: At the planning and design stage, I mentioned earlier how we are bringing together the various regulatory agencies to streamline their processes and to make it easier and more efficient for building developers and their consultants to submit plans and get approvals early.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So, we are taking lead, not just in terms of streamlining of regulatory approvals, but also setting high site productivity targets for our own projects.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: I also spoke about various construction innovations, like Design for Manufacturing and Assembly (DfMA), Prefabricated Prefinished Volumetric Construction (PPVC) and many other techniques.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: These are some techniques that many of our Government agencies are adopting in their own projects.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: I would just like to specifically highlight one, which I think is going to be quite important, because it is not just for new builds.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: I mentioned earlier, that a lot of the total lifecycle cost of a building is in its operations and maintenance phase.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: You can build a building for three years, five years, but you may have to operate and maintain the building for decades.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: And that is where we can make a big difference in terms of efficiency and sustainability targets.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: The public sector is taking the lead in adopting design for maintainability as smart facilities management.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Under the GreenGov.SG initiative, public sector buildings and developments undergoing Addition and Alteration (A&A) works must attain Green Mark Platinum Super Low Energy standards, with a maintainability badge, which are only awarded to projects demonstrating exemplary design for maintainability performance.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: This is significant and public sector buildings above 5,000 square metres are also required to adopt smart FM.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So, in gist, we are walking the talk, we are taking the lead and we are setting high targets for ourselves.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: The second question that the Member had – through all this effort of investing in raising productivity, investing in innovation, whether it leads to a competitive advantage for our firms, for our workers, that can be exported, and can be monetised and can be commercialised abroad?

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: The answer is that we certainly hope so.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: This is one of the objectives that we have, under the refreshed Built Environment Industry Transformation Map (ITM) that we launched last year in September.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Growing our innovation and enterprise ecosystem, in this space, has always been part of our focus in the Built Environment.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: And recent years, we have, in fact, placed more emphasis on translating our research and innovation effort into economic outcomes for commercialisation and export.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We are working very closely as it is an ecosystem approach, with Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs), industry partners, research institutes, and importantly, Government agencies as lead users.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: I will just cite one example, in the interest of time.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Senior Minister of State Tan, can I ask you to make it short.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: I will just cite one example, in the interest of time.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: It is under the Built Environment Technology Alliance, or BETA, programme.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Woh Hup Group and Alliance Concrete Singapore Pte Ltd, in collaboration with the Singapore Institute of Technology (SIT), have developed a manufacturing process for low-carbon concrete.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: This is one of the few in the world that we are trying out, and if successful, this technology could help position companies, like those participating in this project, to better secure overseas construction projects, especially at the time where sustainability and green considerations are at the top of many buyers' minds around the world and our region.

speaker: The Chairman
text: So, I am going to take four more clarifications.

speaker: The Chairman
text: On both sides, can I ask that answers be also kept succinct.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: Just one question for Minister of State Faishal and one for Senior Minister of State Sim Ann.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: I am worried that the cost of this package may be prohibitive for some retirees and may discourage them from applying for CCAs.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: Just to be clear, they could be allowed to opt in later when they need the services.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: And secondly, regarding HDB units with no direct lift access, if lifts cannot be built on each of their floors, would HDB consider installing stair lifts for those units?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: These are widely available and can be folded when not in use, to ensure that there is a wide enough fire escape pathway.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: And I believe it will help many residents with mobility challenges to regain their independence.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Sorry, can I just check with Mr Giam if I got the question correctly.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: He was asking whether we could explore alternative modes for the ease of going up and down stairs, if the lift is not possible, is that right?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Yes, I think the answer is that we will be open to it, but a lot of it depends on the feasibility.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I know this because in my area, at Tiong Bahru, I have a number of flats which fall into that category.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But when you look at the stairs, some of them are curving stairs, and then, the flat stairs are very steep.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But we would have to see what the product actually is.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: My first clarification is, indeed, firmly on wildlife.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: I really would appreciate more clarity on NParks' strategy and proactive approach to managing this more harmoniously in our City in Nature vision, both for the safety of humans as well as animals.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: Is there a step plan or framework in place to preempt hotspots or deescalate conflict, and can more thoughtful design of estates, for example, those near waterways or set in nature, such as Tengah?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: I appreciate public education approach, but I think we really must go beyond campaigns and only responding when there is a wildlife presence, because more animals will be pushed out into sub-optimal territory with more development.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: There have been various challenges faced by Kampong Glam stakeholders in recent times, such as rising costs and also ensuring the commercial viability of their businesses, as well as concerns whether traditional heritage in the area is being eroded by gentrification and newer developments that clash with our culture.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: Will place plan address these sentiments and also explore solutions to balance and address these issues?

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: One important component is how we work with the community.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We have seen good successes where we have worked with community groups.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: For example, I mentioned the Urban Wildlife Group and the Otters Working Group, where we proactively engaged the residents ahead of time, for example, to prepare their facilities better to prevent otters from coming into their homes or minimise the risk or the threat that the otters feel when the young pups are in the habitat.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So, there are many ways we are doing so, and we will continue to do so.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We also see how we can garner effective partnerships and also harness the resources needed.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: One thing about Kampong Glam is that there is this notion of cultural and historical value in that area.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: What we have been doing is we have been working very closely with the businesses there, the investors as well as the community, to see how to find ways to protect Kampong Glam's historical uniqueness.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: While doing that, we also are studying the case studies from around the world to see how some of these cities have been able to protect and continue to make their historical and heritage areas thrive.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: What is key is that I am very heartened that we have got more than 1,600 people coming onboard to share their views.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: This in itself allow us to work very closely with the community.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In fact, even during COVID-19, we worked very closely with the Kampong Glam's community and the people who used live there.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, I am quite happy with the support but now, it is about how we want to navigate together with the community and the stakeholders there to develop and deliver the plan.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Can I ask the Minister does the MND plan to continue to fund this, even if this amount of expenditure continues to goes up?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Two, related to this is, is it fair for the Singapore taxpayer to pay higher taxes to help to fund this expenditure?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Minister, please keep your answer succinct because we are really running close to guillotine time.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: A large part of it has got to do with our building ramp-up.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The land costs, of course, have gone up in this current environment.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will make sure that we spend the resources in order to tackle this issue, in order to provide affordable, accessible housing for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And I think Singaporeans do certainly expect that and that is the response to the second question.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Minister, I referred to the distinction between mature and non-mature BTO flats.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I understand this distinction is currently under review and study.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Can I confirm if this change in nomenclature is something that is being studied as part of the Forward Singapore exercise or is it something for the longer term?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I ask the question because obviously there would be much interest in the impact of the removal of this nomenclature on prices and subsidies.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As part of Forward Singapore Housing Conversations, we have gotten views from Singaporeans as well as from experts about a range of issues pertaining to our public housing system.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Some are of immediate concern, like the current situation; some are longer term considerations such as whether the mature, non-mature estate classification remains relevant.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And so, certainly through the Forward Singapore exercise, we gathered views and are studying the issue.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But all in, MND continues to study how to enhance our public housing system.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Miss Cheryl Chan, do you wish to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: It is probably one of the Ministries that covers and spans so many things: builds into the sky, on land, beyond ground, on lakes and into the sea as well.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: So, I want to thank the entire Ministry, especially the two Ministers, our two Senior Ministers of State as well as Minister of State Faishal and the entire MND team.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: I think the Members have raised very valid issues and also, they have brought up their concerns but they also brought very good suggestions which I think we need to take forward if we want to be able to build in a very sustainable way and also to make sure that we integrate and build a stronger social compact moving forward.
